papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD spans logit-level supervision, representation- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, and specialized adaptations for data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful teacher–student co‑design, KD routinely produces compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. Nonetheless, success depends on signal choice, capacity alignment, data provenance, and attention to robustness, fairness, and distribution shift; several open technical and evaluation questions remain for production deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Effective and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Risks, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of large, high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. KD delivers large gains in inference speed and memory while preserving much of the teacher's utility across NLP tasks (including question answering and sentence understanding) and other modalities. However, naive distillation can transfer undesirable properties such as bias, privacy leakage, or fragility to distribution shift and adversarial attacks. A combination of strategies—student-aware teacher design, multi-teacher curricula, selective sample distillation, data augmentation, adversarial and robust distillation, and privacy-aware ensembles—provides a pragmatic path to compress models while controlling fairness, robustness, and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Principled Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' predictive power. KD is most effective when it goes beyond naïve soft-label copying: matching internal representations, aligning inputs and tokenization, choosing appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and adapting teacher updates or curricula all materially affect transfer quality. KD should be used as part of a broader compression pipeline (architecture design, quantization, pruning, or data strategies) and with explicit checks for rare-token behavior, fairness, and robustness. When applied with these considerations, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for production constraints in vision, language, and other modalities.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Bautista
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System‑Level Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high‑performance models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system‑level strategy—choosing what internal signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures and capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs in vision and language tasks. KD is not a universal remedy: its performance depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of robustness, rare‑token behavior, and bias. I argue KD should be the default first‑line strategy in compression pipelines, but it must be applied as part of a broader, context‑aware toolbox and accompanied by diagnostics and targeted fixes for its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single loss or trick but as a central, context‑aware component of practical model compression pipelines. When treated as a system-level design choice—choosing what signals to transfer, co-designing student architectures, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods like pruning or quantization—KD reliably yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, available data, and distributional considerations, and practitioners must explicitly mitigate failure modes such as propagated teacher errors and loss of rare- or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and System-Level Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive power and support deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, available data, and complementary compression techniques. A pragmatic stance treats KD as the central first-line tool in a broader compression pipeline, combined with pre-training of compact architectures, representation alignment, and targeted interventions for robustness, fairness, and data-limited or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teachers' predictive power. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware alignment, pre-training of compact models, and appropriate data strategies, KD reliably improves inference efficiency while preserving accuracy in many vision and language tasks. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: it requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or heterogeneous data and fairness constraints. Pragmatic deployment therefore treats KD as a first‑line method that must be adapted to task, data, and resource constraints rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Patterns, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods that trains smaller student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost, memory, and latency are reduced while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD spans output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and privacy- or data-aware variants. In practice, KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures and combined with complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful data strategies and augmentation, and curricula that respect student capacity. Remaining challenges include distilling across heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors (especially in language), ensuring robustness and fairness, and operating under privacy or data-limited regimes. This synthesis summarizes prevailing mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical recommendations, and key open problems to guide applied use and future research.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact student models that preserve much of a larger teacher’s accuracy while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD succeeds most reliably when treated as a system-level design choice rather than a single auxiliary loss: practitioners should choose what signals to transfer (logits, features, attention, relations), align student and teacher architectures, incorporate complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and address data limitations through augmentation or data-free/federated strategies. KD has proven value across modalities but also carries risks — optimization difficulties, teacher errors propagated to students, and sensitivity to available data — that require explicit mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring the predictive behavior and internal representations of large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. Treated as a system-level tool and combined with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. Important practical constraints include teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or privacy constraints, and the need to preserve robustness, rare-token behavior, and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically supported path to compress large models into compact, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a central design pattern rather than a single loss term, KD enables multiple transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and online schedules, and integration with architecture-aware design and other compression methods. Practical success requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including pre-training of compact architectures and data augmentation or synthesis), and theoretical understanding of when soft versus hard supervision helps. Framed this way, KD is the most practical, multi-strategy mechanism for real-world compression, provided practitioners pair it with complementary techniques and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary—but Not Sole—Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

A pragmatic stance treats KD as a system-level primitive that should be combined with complementary techniques (data synthesis, representation matching, multi-teacher curricula, and privacy-aware ensembles) to realize reliable, efficient models in real-world NLP and deep learning settings.

However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, and the availability and provenance of data, and it can propagate undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage, fragility) unless paired with targeted design and evaluation. Practitioners should therefore adopt KD as the core of a system‑level compression pipeline that includes architecture‑aware student design, careful selection of distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or multi‑teacher approaches), and explicit validation under distribution shift and fairness/privacy criteria.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central tools for deploying deep models in constrained environments. Work in this area spans simple teacher–student soft-label transfer to advanced feature- and layer-level matching, adversarial and data-free approaches, and automated search guided by distillation. Applications include compressing pre-trained language models, accelerating non-autoregressive translation, compressing generative models, and improving low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical studies highlight both practical recipes (mixing hard and soft labels, many-to-many layer mappings, feature mimicking) and conceptual explanations (connections to label smoothing and regularization), while open challenges remain in retaining rare-token behavior, mitigating bias transfer, and scaling distillation to privacy- or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Methods, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or aggregated multi-teacher signals—KD enables compact models that retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware changes). KD also adapts to constrained settings (limited or private data, domain-specialization, federated or black-box teachers) but requires careful design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and training curricula. When applied as part of a principled compression pipeline, KD offers a practical route to deployable high-quality models, though open problems remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, robustness, and reliable operation under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models so that deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints becomes practical. KD encompasses a family of techniques — from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure — and is commonly combined with complementary compressions such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows that, when matched to student capacity and data availability, distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data access (including data-free alternatives), and robustness or fairness requirements; remaining challenges concern principled objective design, optimization under capacity mismatch, and reliable transfer of robustness and rare-token/long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has grown into a flexible toolkit that includes soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-representation and attention matching, multi- and online-teacher schemes, self-distillation, and data strategies ranging from use of original corpora to synthetic or data-free generation. When carefully matched to student capacity and paired with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely produces compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance. Remaining challenges center on data scarcity and privacy, cross-domain and rare-token transfer, robustness and fairness, and principled choices about what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Contexts, and Required Safeguards
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is applied as a design pipeline—choosing what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational maps), aligning teacher and student architectures, and adapting data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation)—it routinely produces compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is context dependent: success hinges on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity and architecture, data provenance and availability, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-class behavior. Treating KD as a first-line tool combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and targeted mitigations for its limits yields practical, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. KD offers multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals) and can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful design choices; KD should therefore be treated as a core element of a compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in constrained environments. KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and structural inductive biases; it supports multi-teacher, progressive, adversarial, and data-constrained variants; and it can be combined with architecture-aware design and data strategies to improve efficiency, robustness, and domain adaptability. While highly effective in practice, KD's success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and the availability and suitability of data, so it should be treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, attention/relational signals, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or synthesized-data variants—that often recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what and how to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior. KD therefore functions best as a central component within a broader compression and deployment pipeline rather than as a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Foundation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible path to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Through a variety of transfer targets and training schedules, KD enables major reductions in parameter count, memory use, and latency while often preserving most of a teacher’s task performance. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student pre-training and capacity, availability or synthesis of data, and complementary compression steps. KD is best treated as a toolkit to be combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and evaluation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, and generation tasks. Contemporary KD methods extend far beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, curriculum and online schemes, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and tight integrations with architecture-level compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends on matched teacher–student design, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthetic-data alternatives, and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-class behaviors. Open challenges remain in domain-shift robustness, privacy-sensitive distillation, automated student architecture design, and principled selection of which aspects of teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable framework for producing compact models by transferring behavior from larger teachers to smaller students. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource constraints, and it extends beyond simple logit matching to include feature-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its efficacy depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled information, data availability, capacity mismatch, and fairness or robustness concerns. A considered KD pipeline—combining soft-targets, internal representation guidance, task-aware objectives, and suitable data strategies—yields robust, efficient students fitting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Practical, Theoretical, and Methodological Evidence for Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and mature approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from richer teacher models to compact students. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, vision, graph learning, and retrieval—KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher's performance. Beyond pure compression, KD variants address practical deployment concerns: multi-teacher and confidence-aware schemes improve robustness to imperfect teachers; progressive and module-level replacement approaches enable deeper integrated compression; online/distillation-in-parallel techniques scale training and improve reproducibility; and targeted feature-distillation methods refine representational quality. Theory of wide networks provides guidance on when soft labels help and when mixing hard labels is beneficial. Together, empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a versatile, well-grounded toolbox for model compression and knowledge transfer in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or multi-modal models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural insights. Research has developed diverse KD variants—soft-label distillation, internal and layer-wise imitation, task-aware filtering, data-free distillation, and architecture-search guided compression—each addressing optimization, data availability, or deployment constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs between matching teacher outputs and student generalization, the value of pre-training compact models, and the importance of choosing what and how knowledge is transferred to maximize downstream task performance while meeting resource limits.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-line, Context-aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred, how intermediate layers are aligned, and whether data or privacy constraints hold, KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in inference speed and memory. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: optimization difficulties, mismatches in capacity between teacher and student, and limited or private data require tailored objectives, architecture-aware choices, and complementary techniques. This essay argues KD should be a primary strategy in model-compression toolkits while recommending concrete practices to increase reliability across real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of their predictive performance. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners use KD to achieve lower latency, smaller memory footprints, and easier deployment under resource, privacy, or heterogeneity constraints. Effective distillation combines choices about which knowledge to transfer (logits, features, attention maps), how to align teacher and student layers, how to generate or select training data, and how to adapt architectures to task requirements. While KD often succeeds when paired with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture search, ensembling, data augmentation), its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, and targeted objectives that reflect downstream tasks. Recognizing the mechanisms and limits of KD helps practitioners design robust compression pipelines that balance efficiency, accuracy, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Crawford
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher‑student recipe into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and explicitly addressing robustness and distributional shifts. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, training regimes, practical recommendations, and remaining challenges for KD-driven model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for making large neural models deployable: by transferring richer supervision from high-capacity teacher models to compact students, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving or even improving generalization. Best results arise when distillation strategies are matched to deployment constraints and student capacity—combining logits and representational objectives, co-designing teacher and student, using appropriate data-augmentation or synthetic-data strategies, and integrating structural compression like pruning or module replacement. Although challenges remain (teacher imperfections, low-frequency token fidelity, data-free settings, and distribution shift), a set of practical, complementary methods yields robust pathways to efficient models across NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teacher networks. KD leverages multiple forms of transferred information—soft outputs, internal representations, attention or relational signals—and is most effective when co‑designed with student architectures and combined with complementary compression methods. While KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision, language, and recommendation tasks, it is not a universal solution: reliable compression requires attention to teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and robustness under distribution shift. I argue that KD should be treated as a context‑sensitive, system‑level primitive: valuable and broadly applicable when integrated into a tailored compression pipeline, but reliant on careful design and explicit mitigation of its known limitations.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: The Role and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. KD is applicable across modalities and tasks, from machine translation and reading comprehension to distributed training and privacy-sensitive deployment. Success depends on aligning teacher and student representations, selecting appropriate knowledge (logits, intermediate features, attention, contrastive signals), and matching methods to constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, or privacy requirements. Theoretical analyses and practical advances both show that careful design choices — including attention-based matching, layer projection, task-aware filtering, online collaboration, multi-teacher weighting, and privacy-aware perturbation — materially affect outcomes and trade-offs between fidelity, efficiency, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD is both a compression mechanism and a training-time regularizer: when carefully designed it preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer (outputs, intermediate features, or both), how to align teacher and student architectures, what data are used (real, augmented, or synthetic), and whether deployment constraints (privacy, heterogeneity, federated settings) limit access to teacher data or models. A principled KD practice adapts targets, aligns representations where useful, addresses teacher–student mismatches, and recognizes scenarios where KD alone is insufficient.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention or relational supervision, multi- or self-teaching schedules, and data-aware or data-free protocols—and is most effective when co-designed with student architectures and complementary compression methods. Practical application requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, data access or synthesis, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When integrated with task-aware student design, data or augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD reliably reduces memory, compute, and latency while preserving—or sometimes improving—accuracy and specific properties (e.g., robustness or multimodal capabilities). This paper argues that KD should be treated as the primary, adaptable instrument in model-compression toolkits for practical deep-learning and NLP systems, and outlines concrete mechanisms and caveats for its application.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple softened-target matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online regimes, adversarial decision-boundary techniques, and data-aware or data-free strategies. When integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility and data provenance, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Important limitations remain, including sensitivity to distribution shift, data- and privacy-constrained settings, preserving long-tail behaviors, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher biases; addressing these issues requires pipeline-oriented, context-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Gutierrez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. A family of distillation targets and training regimes—soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-constrained or data-free strategies—has emerged and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical practice shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance when teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and objective design are chosen deliberately; remaining gaps include reliable data-free distillation, preserving rare/low-frequency behaviors, robustness under domain shift, and principled guidance for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and natural language processing. When integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Effective application requires deliberate choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle limited or domain-shifted data, and how to audit robustness and rare-token behavior. Treated as a first-line, context-aware tool rather than a one-size-fits-all cure, KD enables practical deployments while highlighting research directions around robustness, privacy, and heterogeneous-architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal information from teacher models. A diverse set of distillation objectives and training regimes—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature or attention alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, adversarial or data-free variants, and task- or device-aware architecture search—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and augmentation, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques; open problems remain in theoretical explanation, cross-distribution robustness, and preserving rare-token or fairness-sensitive behavior.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely used approach to compressing large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods span soft-logit matching, ensemble distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and privacy- or data-aware variants. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show that carefully chosen distillation targets and student–teacher alignment can achieve large reductions in inference cost with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in performance. However, practical success depends on capacity-matching, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, degraded rare-token behavior in NLP, and privacy concerns. KD performs best as a component of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture choices, pruning/quantization, and data-centric strategies.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for producing compact, efficient deep models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller students. Across domains — vision, generation, control, and natural language tasks — KD enables large portions of teacher performance to be retained while enabling dramatic reductions in inference cost, memory footprint, and power consumption. When used thoughtfully (choice of distillation signal, teacher–student compatibility, and data strategy), KD integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and privacy- or data-constrained workflows to produce production-ready compact models. Equally important are mitigations for risks such as bias transfer, degraded robustness under domain shift, and failures when original training data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Thornton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default first‑line strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students because it consistently yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, is methodologically flexible, and composes well with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, and the availability and provenance of data, and it can propagate undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage, fragility) unless paired with targeted design and evaluation. Practitioners should therefore adopt KD as the core of a system‑level compression pipeline that includes architecture‑aware student design, careful selection of distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or multi‑teacher approaches), and explicit validation under distribution shift and fairness/privacy criteria.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as the practical core of model compression for deep learning and NLP: a multifaceted toolkit that reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when combined with careful design choices. KD succeeds because it can transfer soft predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and relational structure, and because it composes naturally with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, and privacy-preserving proxies). However, KD is not a universal cure — its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, access to appropriate data (or viable data-free alternatives), and explicit handling of robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy constraints. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a core, configurable element of compression pipelines and pair it with targeted engineering, diagnostics, and domain-aware choices to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the original model's utility. Empirical results across vision, language, recommendation, and generation tasks show that carefully designed distillation—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate feature and relational transfer, online co-training, and progressive module replacement—enables large reductions in latency and memory with modest accuracy loss. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and augmentation, and targeted mitigation of risks such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, and privacy leakage. Treating KD as a system-level primitive and combining it with complementary compression and data strategies yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Rationale, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, flexible pathway to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Treated as a system-level toolkit rather than a single loss term, KD supports multiple transfer channels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Successful deployment requires careful teacher–student alignment, data or synthetic-data strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-token or fine-grained behavior. I argue KD should be the default first‑line strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP while being applied deliberately and combined with complementary compression primitives and validation under realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive power. The approach spans simple logit matching to richer supervision such as intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial and online schemes, curriculum-driven supervision, and multi-teacher or self-distillation variants. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks, but its success depends on what is transferred, the data used for distillation, and procedures that preserve robustness and domain generalization. Key challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, data scarcity or absence, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods that transfers richer supervision from large teacher models to compact students in order to reduce inference cost while retaining predictive performance. KD covers logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, channel- and feature-level transfers, self- and online-distillation, and multi-teacher and data-free variants. Its effectiveness depends on alignment between teacher and student capacity, the choice of what to transfer, data availability, and deployment constraints; therefore KD should be treated as a central component of modern compression pipelines but always applied with task- and context-aware adaptations and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation trains smaller, faster student models to emulate larger teacher models, reducing inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade KD has diversified from soft-target matching into a toolkit that includes logits and feature matching, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. KD is most effective when matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints and is typically combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design). Important limitations remain—teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, data scarcity, and robustness/fairness concerns—motivating careful evaluation and hybrid or task-aware approaches for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Allen

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted strategy to produce smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact student models. The effectiveness of KD depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility and capacity, availability or synthesis of training data, and integration with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Remaining practical challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors for sequence tasks, privacy-sensitive distillation, and automated co-design of students and distillation objectives.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Constraints, and Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models or otherwise reduce model size while retaining performance. Core approaches include matching teacher soft-targets, aligning intermediate representations (features, attention), and combining distillation with structural compression (pruning, quantization) or automated architecture design. Practical uses span on-device deployment, task-adaptive compression, lifelong and continual learning, robustness preservation, and privacy-aware or data-free scenarios. Success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (or synthesis), and training protocols; addressing these factors via complementary strategies yields the best accuracy–efficiency trade-offs while exposing open challenges in robustness, fairness, and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied model compression technique that trains a compact student model to emulate a larger teacher (or ensemble) so that inference cost and storage are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD has been adapted across domains (vision, graphs, NLP, multimodal systems) and combined with other compression methods; it can transfer logits, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge, and it can be extended to multi-teacher, self-distillation, and privacy-aware settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves generalization but also reveals limits and failure modes that motivate augmented objectives, data strategies, and teacher-training methods to achieve more effective, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Baker

However, distillation is not automatic: outcomes depend on teacher strength and training, student architecture and capacity, the form of distilled signals, data availability (including data‑free settings), and fairness/privacy goals. Best practice treats KD as a core component combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and deployment-aware procedures to produce reliable, efficient models for real applications.

papers_seen.author: Terry

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature family of methods that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students retain much of the teacher’s performance while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Remaining challenges include reliably preserving long-tail or rare behaviors in NLP, distilling without original data, avoiding transfer of teacher biases, and characterizing performance under domain shift.

By combining architectural mapping, task-aware selection of distilled signals, dynamic teacher weighting, and online or data-free schemes, KD enables deployment of strong models in latency-, compute-, and privacy-constrained settings while exposing clear directions for further research.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are essential tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. A wide family of methods — from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature transfer, projector-based alignment, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning or architecture search — let practitioners trade compute and memory for modest accuracy loss. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on optimization, data alignment, and the choice of distilled signals; it can replicate undesirable teacher behaviors and fails when teacher–student mismatch or data constraints are not addressed. Practical deployment therefore requires selecting KD variants that match application constraints and combining distillation with complementary compression and robustness techniques.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (and How to Use It Well)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, empirically grounded approach that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. When treated as a system-level tool and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), distillation produces compact models suitable for real deployments across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. However, distillation is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, availability and provenance of data (including options for data-free or few-shot settings), and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. Practitioners should therefore adopt distillation as a central but context-aware element of an integrated compression pipeline and use targeted diagnostics and mitigation for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving task performance. The field encompasses soft-label (logit) supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, structural and architectural transformations, data-free and privacy-aware variants, multi-teacher and online distillation, and meta-learned teacher strategies. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves student generalization and enables deployment under resource constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on what signals are transferred, data availability and provenance, optimization dynamics, and teacher–student capacity gaps. Practical deployment requires choosing student architectures, distillation signals, and training regimes aligned to the target task and constraints; key open problems include robust data-free distillation, principled teacher design, and theoretical characterization of when different knowledge sources help.

papers_seen.author: Mccann
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive signals, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. KD is most effective when chosen signals, student architecture, and data strategies are matched to the task and deployment context and when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Important open problems remain around theory, robustness under distribution shift, preserving fine-grained or rare behaviors in language tasks, data-scarce or privacy-sensitive scenarios, and automated student design. This paper synthesizes empirical practices, mechanisms, theoretical insights, and practical guidance from recent studies to orient research and engineering choices for KD-based compression.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. KD spans logit-level supervision, representation- and attention-level matching, ensemble and online schemes, and data-free or synthetic-data variants. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student co-design, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; distribution shift, rare-token behaviors, privacy, and data-free settings remain important challenges that benefit from hybrid pipelines and targeted engineering.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Weeks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, system‑level starting point for compressing large models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When designed as an integrated pipeline—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, combining with pretraining and complementary compression techniques, and adopting appropriate data strategies—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. Responsible application requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and robustness to distributional shift and rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, deployable models. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, KD has been used to reduce inference cost while retaining most of the teacher model's performance. Research has advanced along several complementary axes: (1) methods that shape what is transferred (logits, hidden representations, attention or task-specific signals), (2) how the transfer is performed (layer-wise, multi-teacher, adversarial or student-aware training), (3) strategies to cope with limited or no access to original training data, and (4) techniques that preserve privacy and improve training efficiency. These lines of work show that careful alignment of objectives, attention to capacity gaps between teacher and student, and tailoring distillation to task and data regimes are critical for effective compression. Remaining challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, principled selection of what to distill for a target task, and maintaining robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Hybrid Recipe
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces parameter count, latency, and memory footprint while preserving much of teacher behavior when applied with attention to what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, and data constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its outcomes depend on student capacity, data availability and match, privacy requirements, and objective design. For robust, production-ready compression, KD should be treated as the central component of a hybrid pipeline that deliberately combines distillation with architecture-aware pruning, quantization, data strategies, and teacher design choices.
