papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for converting large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teacher’s capability while improving latency, memory, and energy efficiency. KD works through multiple channels (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, attention or relational signals, and multi‑teacher regimes) and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. However, KD is not a one‑size‑fits‑all solution: its success depends on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation strategies, and careful evaluation of robustness, privacy, and distributional shifts. When treated as a central element of an integrated compression pipeline and applied with explicit safeguards and complementary techniques, KD reliably yields compact models suited for real‑world deployment.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation can be combined with architectural replacement, layer mapping, and task-adaptive search to produce compact models that meet latency and capacity constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, data complexity, and which examples or representations are used for transfer; naive application can propagate teacher errors or harm low-frequency predictions. Careful design—using task-aware compression, selective or mixed supervision, and targeted remedies for dataset artifacts—enables distillation to deliver efficient, robust models for real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of methods for converting large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. Across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks, practitioners apply a spectrum of KD objectives — from softened-logit supervision to representation and relation matching, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and data-free approaches — and combine KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when teacher–student capacity, data availability, and the form of transferred signal are well matched. Open challenges include theoretical characterization of transfer, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors in language models, robust distillation under domain shift, and privacy-aware or data-free compression regimes.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks KD variants—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention patterns, multi-teacher and progressive schemes, and self-distillation—have enabled compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success typically requires co-design of the distillation signal, student architecture, data and augmentation choices, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., quantization or pruning). Persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, handling limited or private data, preserving rare-token and robustness properties, and automating trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Outcomes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Approaches vary from matching final soft targets to transferring intermediate representations, leveraging ensembles or multiple teachers, to data-free synthesis and combining KD with pruning or low-precision numerics. In NLP, KD has enabled compact models to approach the performance of large pre-trained models while substantially reducing inference cost. Recent work clarifies theoretical mechanisms, proposes many-to-many layer alignment techniques, and develops adaptive multi-teacher weighting and zero-shot distillation to broaden applicability. Despite strong empirical gains, open challenges remain in task-specific alignment, robustness to heterogeneous data, and preserving fairness and calibration during compression.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses supervising students with softened teacher outputs as well as transferring intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization protocols, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Important open challenges include handling data-poor or data-free settings, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage), and reliably transferring rare or fine-grained knowledge across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers in both vision and natural language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints, and many variants extend KD beyond soft-target transfer to feature matching, multi-teacher schemes, progressive replacement, and domain-adaptive workflows. At the same time, theoretical and empirical analyses reveal optimization barriers, sensitivity to the choice of data and teacher signals, and imperfect matching between teacher and student as important limits. This review argues that KD is a powerful but context-dependent tool: its success requires matching the distillation signal to student capacity and task complexity, combining KD with complementary compression techniques, and paying careful attention to data and training dynamics to avoid degenerate outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Haney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Pipeline‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven toolkit for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple channels of supervision — softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals — and interoperates well with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. However, KD is not a standalone cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, what and how signals are transferred, data availability (or synthetic/data‑free strategies), and explicit checks for robustness, rare‑token behavior, and fairness. Careful co‑design of students, selection of distillation targets, and integration of KD into a broader compression pipeline yield the most reliable outcomes for deep learning and NLP deployment.

papers_seen.author: Dalton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied deliberately — choosing what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining KD with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search — KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, data availability (including data‑free or privacy‑constrained scenarios), and careful design around teacher–student mismatch and task-specific objectives. Responsible, task-aware application of KD, integrated into system-level compression pipelines, produces the most reliable operational outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Core, Methods, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for converting large pretrained models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. When applied with attention to what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how teacher and student are aligned (architecture-aware objectives, projectors, layer selection), and how data constraints are handled (data augmentation, data-free synthesis, privacy-aware workflows), KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across NLP and multimodal tasks. Nevertheless, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, and robustness under distribution shift, so practitioners should pair KD with complementary compression tools and task-aware evaluations to deploy compact models reliably.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Limits, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones that are deployable in resource-constrained settings. A rich set of distillation strategies has been developed: matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations, adversarial or data-free synthesis of training examples, multi-teacher aggregation, and contrastive or projector-based representation alignment. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many tasks (including NLP and graph learning), but practical success depends strongly on optimization details, the availability and alignment of data, and careful design of the distillation objective. Privacy-preserving variants and methods tailored to domain-specific architectures (e.g., GNNs, transformers) extend KD’s applicability, while also introducing trade-offs between utility, robustness, and guarantees. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical findings, and known limitations to guide research and practice in KD for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD is both a compression mechanism and a training-time regularizer: when carefully designed it preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer (outputs, intermediate features, or both), how to align teacher and student architectures, what data are used (real, augmented, or synthetic), and whether deployment constraints (privacy, heterogeneity, federated settings) limit access to teacher data or models. A principled KD practice adapts targets, aligns representations where useful, addresses teacher–student mismatches, and recognizes scenarios where KD alone is insufficient.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking large models: it is a versatile family of techniques that can preserve performance while enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but it must be adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. Effective KD requires attention to the teacher-student relationship (including training teachers that are "student-friendly"), to data availability (including data-free approaches), and to distributional mismatches (e.g., federated or heterogeneous-device scenarios). When such concerns are addressed—via task-adaptive compression, feature- or relation-aware transfer, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, or methods that expose raw data signals lost in naive distillation—KD can deliver near-teacher performance at far lower cost. However, KD has known failure modes (such as propagating teacher errors on low-frequency tokens or degrading under data heterogeneity) that demand targeted remedies. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an adaptable design pattern: choose techniques that match your downstream objective (accuracy, latency, privacy, heterogeneity) rather than applying a one-size-fits-all distillation loss.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable tool for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. When combined with complementary practices — careful teacher selection or adaptation, pre-training of compact architectures, feature-level matching, and privacy- or data-aware workflows — KD yields most of the practical benefits of compression while exposing clear trade-offs and failure modes. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the backbone of model compression pipelines, but that realizing reliable production gains requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The field encompasses logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, multi-teacher and online regimes, data-free or privacy-aware variants, and architecture-aware pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or automated architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD commonly recovers most of a teacher’s performance while delivering substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and energy, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, and available data. Open problems remain around domain shift, preserving fine-grained behaviors (e.g., rare tokens), robustness, and principled data-free or privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational alignment—consistently enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while recovering much of teacher accuracy when applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization dynamics. Practical KD pipelines typically combine distilled signals with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adopt data-aware strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols) to address real-world deployment challenges. Key open problems include robustly preserving long-tail or rare behaviors, handling distribution shift and privacy constraints, and automating student design for strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with careful teacher–student design, choice of distilled signals, and complementary compression primitives, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of the original model’s predictive power. However, the technique is not universally sufficient: its success depends on data access and provenance, teacher quality and student capacity, and targeted handling of robustness, rare behaviors, and privacy or domain constraints. Framing KD as a system-level primitive and combining it with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and evaluation under realistic deployment constraints yields the most reliable path to compact, effective models.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, broadly applicable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their predictive power. KD enables large gains in inference speed, reduced memory footprint, and practical deployment under latency, compute, and privacy constraints. However, straightforward distillation can transfer undesirable properties and can underperform when data is limited or teacher–student mismatches are large. To realize KD's full potential practitioners should combine soft-target transfer with representation matching, targeted data augmentation or data-free synthesis, careful teacher design (including ensembles or student-aware teachers), and explicit robustness or privacy-aware objectives. These combined practices produce compact models that are accurate, efficient, and more robust for real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, attention/relational signals, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or synthesized-data variants—that often recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what and how to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior. KD therefore functions best as a central component within a broader compression and deployment pipeline rather than as a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Massey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Contextual Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system-level tool—combined with architecture-aware design, complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and tailored data strategies—KD routinely enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the provenance and amount of data used for transfer, and careful evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy. This paper argues that KD should be the central component of practical compression pipelines, and it outlines mechanisms, practical dependencies, common failure modes, and design recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Crawford
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher‑student recipe into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and explicitly addressing robustness and distributional shifts. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, training regimes, practical recommendations, and remaining challenges for KD-driven model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical tool for compressing large models into efficient students while acknowledging that its effectiveness depends critically on task, data, teacher–student alignment, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data strategies), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, but reliable production use requires deliberate signal selection, capacity-aware alignment, and privacy- or data-sensitive adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Contexts, and Required Safeguards
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is applied as a design pipeline—choosing what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational maps), aligning teacher and student architectures, and adapting data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation)—it routinely produces compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is context dependent: success hinges on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity and architecture, data provenance and availability, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-class behavior. Treating KD as a first-line tool combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and targeted mitigations for its limits yields practical, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often ensemble or higher-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to improve accuracy, robustness, interpretability, or resource efficiency. Over the past decade KD has been adapted beyond the original soft-label logits transfer: methods now target intermediate features, attention maps, channel-wise signals, and training curricula; they address deployment constraints such as low-precision arithmetic, absence of original data, heterogeneous device models, and federated settings. In NLP, distillation has been applied to compress pretrained language models, to enable multi-task or lifelong learning, and to improve robustness in tasks such as question answering and machine translation. Practical recipes combine architectural adjustments, selective or staged distillation, and application-specific modifications to retain teacher strengths while avoiding transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for producing compact models that preserve much of larger teachers’ performance when applied with task- and deployment-aware design. KD encompasses a family of objectives and training regimes — from softened-logit supervision to intermediate representation matching, ensembles, online distillation, and data-free variants — and is most effective when integrated into system-level pipelines that include architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data strategies. Real-world success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing data limitations and privacy, and evaluating robustness to distribution shift and rare or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Patterns, and Practical Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit that transfers richer supervision from larger or heterogeneous teacher models into smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining task performance. KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), composes with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), and can be adapted to domain-specific settings (generative models, recommenders, distributed training). Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data alignment, choice of signals to transfer, and mitigation strategies for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy. When applied with principled design—matching distilled signals to student capacity, using teacher-aware curricula, and combining with other compression tools—KD frequently yields production-ready efficiency gains, but it is not a universal remedy and requires careful engineering to avoid failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are essential tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. A wide family of methods — from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature transfer, projector-based alignment, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning or architecture search — let practitioners trade compute and memory for modest accuracy loss. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on optimization, data alignment, and the choice of distilled signals; it can replicate undesirable teacher behaviors and fails when teacher–student mismatch or data constraints are not addressed. Practical deployment therefore requires selecting KD variants that match application constraints and combining distillation with complementary compression and robustness techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational alignment—consistently enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while recovering much of teacher accuracy when applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization dynamics. Practical KD pipelines typically combine distilled signals with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adopt data-aware strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols) to address real-world deployment challenges. Key open problems include robustly preserving long-tail or rare behaviors, handling distribution shift and privacy constraints, and automating student design for strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (and How to Use It Well)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, empirically grounded approach that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. When treated as a system-level tool and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), distillation produces compact models suitable for real deployments across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. However, distillation is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, availability and provenance of data (including options for data-free or few-shot settings), and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. Practitioners should therefore adopt distillation as a central but context-aware element of an integrated compression pipeline and use targeted diagnostics and mitigation for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When integrated with task-aware student design, data or augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD reliably reduces memory, compute, and latency while preserving—or sometimes improving—accuracy and specific properties (e.g., robustness or multimodal capabilities). This paper argues that KD should be treated as the primary, adaptable instrument in model-compression toolkits for practical deep-learning and NLP systems, and outlines concrete mechanisms and caveats for its application.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervisory signals richer than hard labels. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD has matured into a flexible toolkit that includes logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware variants. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when the distillation protocol is chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Open challenges remain in data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, preserving rare-token and long-tail behaviors, avoiding propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors (biases or brittleness), and guaranteeing robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques constitute a flexible toolkit for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. Across speech, vision, and natural language tasks, practitioners transfer predictive behavior and selected internal structure from teachers to students to reduce latency, memory, and energy while preserving task performance. The literature shows a spectrum of methods (soft-targets, representation matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free approaches), trade-offs that depend on student capacity and data access, and practical strategies that pair distillation with pretraining, architecture design, and data interventions. Important limitations remain around domain shift, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, theoretical characterization of what transfers, and privacy-aware or data-free distillation regimes.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Powerful but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Its effectiveness arises from the ability to transfer different forms of knowledge (soft labels, intermediate features, attention, ensembles) and to combine distillation with data augmentation, pretraining, and task-aware objectives. However, KD is not uniformly successful: outcomes depend on teacher-student capacity alignment, the choice of distillation targets, data availability and augmentation strategy, and deployment constraints such as privacy or device heterogeneity. Careful selection of distillation signals, task-aware layer matching, and augmentation or synthetic-data strategies improve robustness; conversely, mismatches in architecture, domain shift, or heterogeneous federated settings can sharply limit benefits.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for converting large teacher models into compact, deployable students. When applied as a context-aware, system-level strategy and combined with complementary methods (architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for NLP and broader deep-learning tasks. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and careful evaluation of robustness, rare-token behaviors, and privacy. Treating KD as the first-line tool within an integrated compression pipeline—rather than a one-size-fits-all loss—delivers the most reliable outcomes while pointing to open research on robustness, data-free distillation, and privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for converting large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teacher’s capability while improving latency, memory, and energy efficiency. KD works through multiple channels (soft targets, intermediate representation matching, attention or relational signals, and multi‑teacher regimes) and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. However, KD is not a one‑size‑fits‑all solution: its success depends on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation strategies, and careful evaluation of robustness, privacy, and distributional shifts. When treated as a central element of an integrated compression pipeline and applied with explicit safeguards and complementary techniques, KD reliably yields compact models suited for real‑world deployment.

papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the original performance. KD has proven effective across modalities and tasks, and modern practice extends beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, data-free approaches, and training-time strategies that make teachers more amenable to transfer. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: distribution shifts, limited or absent training data, teacher–student mismatch, and adversarial concerns require complementary techniques and careful design. When combined with task-aware selection of distilled signals, student-friendly teacher training, and data- or representation-aware remedies, KD becomes a practical backbone for deployment under latency, compute, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention imitation, relational and ensemble signals, and data-aware variants (including synthesized or data-free approaches). In practice, KD is usually combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, or architecture search) and student-aware training practices (pretraining, capacity alignment, and data augmentation) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical results show distilled students can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but open challenges remain in data-scarce and privacy-sensitive regimes, preserving fine-grained or rare behaviors, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Malone
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolkit for Model Compression — Practical, Powerful, but Not Sufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, practical toolkit for compressing deep and language models: it provides flexible supervision channels that routinely yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is context dependent and not a standalone cure; its effectiveness hinges on what signals are transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and explicit checks for robustness and distributional shift. Effective deployment requires composing KD with complementary compression methods, careful co‑design of teacher and student, and evaluation under realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller or otherwise constrained models. Approaches span from matching outputs to mimicking intermediate representations, from layer-aware mapping strategies to task-adaptive architecture search, and include protocols for heterogeneous, data-constrained, or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical results across vision and language tasks demonstrate strong gains in efficiency with modest drops (or even improvements) in performance, while persistent challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, choosing appropriate sources of knowledge, and designing robust data-free or federated distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: The Centrality of Knowledge Distillation in Modern Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision and language tasks, distillation can act both as a compression mechanism and as a regularizer, and it integrates naturally with complementary strategies such as architecture search, layer-wise alignment, representation matching, data augmentation, pruning, and deployment-aware methods. When applied thoughtfully—matching teacher and student representations, tuning the signal provided by soft labels, and adapting to task or device constraints—distillation enables practical, high-performing compressed models suitable for production and edge settings.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring rich supervisory signals beyond hard labels. KD has evolved from simple logits-matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate representation alignment, attention and relational matching, online and self-distillation, data‑free synthesis, and teacher‑training strategies that improve transfer. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data and architecture choices, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. Practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as bias transfer, degraded robustness under distribution shift, and privacy leakage. Important open problems include automating objective and architecture selection, preserving rare or safety‑critical behaviors, and scalable data‑free distillation for complex tasks.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple softened-target matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online regimes, adversarial decision-boundary techniques, and data-aware or data-free strategies. When integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility and data provenance, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Important limitations remain, including sensitivity to distribution shift, data- and privacy-constrained settings, preserving long-tail behaviors, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher biases; addressing these issues requires pipeline-oriented, context-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and distributed settings KD often recovers much of a teacher's predictive performance while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and deployment under resource or privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: outcomes depend on what signals are transferred (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, availability and quality of data (including data-free or federated setups), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats distillation as one element of a compression pipeline that combines representation matching, architecture-aware student design, data strategies, and risk-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of techniques that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and compute while preserving task performance. KD methods range from transferring softened teacher outputs to matching intermediate representations or relational structure, and they are applied across modalities including language, vision, speech, and multimodal architectures. Practical deployments combine KD with architecture-aware transformations, low-precision numerics, data synthesis, and multi-stage training to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, and privacy. While KD often yields strong empirical gains, success depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability and provenance, student architecture design, and optimization strategy; core open problems include handling teacher errors, preserving rare or fine-grained behavior, and reliably distilling across domain or architecture gaps.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation can be combined with architectural replacement, layer mapping, and task-adaptive search to produce compact models that meet latency and capacity constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, data complexity, and which examples or representations are used for transfer; naive application can propagate teacher errors or harm low-frequency predictions. Careful design—using task-aware compression, selective or mixed supervision, and targeted remedies for dataset artifacts—enables distillation to deliver efficient, robust models for real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile paradigm for transferring knowledge from larger or more informative teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods extend beyond soft-target (logit) matching to include intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and matched to deployment constraints, KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes dominant mechanisms, common variants, practical guidance, representative applications, and open challenges for KD-driven model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable design paradigm—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely achieves strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher quality, and evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints; practitioners should therefore apply KD together with targeted validation, robustness checks, and complementary engineering such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is matched to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch. When designers select what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to expose the student to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online peer predictions), and how to adapt protocols for distributed or privacy-sensitive settings, KD yields large practical gains in latency, memory, and deployability while controlling risks such as bias transfer or robustness loss. A deployment-aware KD practice leverages representation-aware objectives, data-free synthesis when training data are unavailable, adversarial or online schemes for richer alignment, and federated-distillation architectures for communication-efficient collaboration.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD spans matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and transferring relational or ensemble knowledge; it can be combined with data synthesis or data-free approaches and integrated with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Empirical evidence across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows KD often yields strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs, but its effectiveness is context dependent and requires explicit attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and robustness considerations.
