papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible supervision (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensemble signals) and interoperates with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data synthesis). When used systematically—selecting what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, leveraging data-aware or data-free strategies, and integrating KD into broader compression pipelines—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployments. At the same time, careful attention to teacher quality, rare-token preservation, robustness, and domain shift is required to avoid predictable failure modes and to maximize real-world utility.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A diverse set of KD mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data synthesis—has been developed and combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many vision and language tasks, while remaining sensitive to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, domain shift, and robustness concerns. Practical pipelines therefore co-design student architectures, distillation targets, and data handling strategies to achieve the best trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central model-compression approach that trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost, memory, and deployment barriers are reduced while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive behavior. Research has produced a family of distillation objectives (soft-targets, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational losses), training regimes (offline, online, self-distillation, multi-teacher), and system-level integrations (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical studies show well-designed distillation pipelines commonly recover a large fraction of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization, but success depends on what knowledge is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical use therefore combines algorithmic choices with architecture-aware compression and data strategies tailored to the task and environment.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when its objectives, data, and student architectures are co-designed with deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality and alignment, student capacity, data provenance (including data-free scenarios), and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy. I argue KD should be treated as the core component of compression pipelines while being combined with complementary techniques and careful evaluation under realistic deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can approach the performance of larger ones while meeting deployment constraints. KD methods vary in the form of transferred knowledge, how alignment is performed, and whether additional strategies (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) are used; empirical results show broad effectiveness across modalities but reveal important limitations and open problems around data availability, robustness, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, System-Level Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations and relational cues—KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with deployment-aware architecture and data choices. KD should be treated as a central, configurable element of compression pipelines: highly effective in many settings but requiring complementary methods and careful design to address data limits, teacher–student mismatch, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone for Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible toolkit for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free training. When combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student design, KD produces practical accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs for vision, language, and multimodal systems. However, the method’s success is context-dependent: it requires attention to teacher quality and bias, student capacity and architecture compatibility, data provenance and synthesis, and robustness under distributional shift. This synthesis argues that KD should be treated as a central, system-level primitive in compression pipelines but implemented with task-aware choices and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD operates at multiple levels — softened output distributions, intermediate feature or attention imitation, and relational or layer-wise alignment — and composes naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD yields substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy for deployed systems, but its success depends on careful design choices related to what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Practical deployment treats KD as a core element of a hybrid compression pipeline, with task-aware signal selection, student-aware teacher design, and targeted remedies for distribution shift, low-frequency phenomena, adversarial vulnerability, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of methods to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models. KD methods include softened-logit supervision, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data‑constrained or data‑free protocols. In practice KD is most effective when co‑designed with student architecture choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, distribution shift, and privacy. Key open problems include principled teacher design, reliable data-free distillation, theoretical characterization of transfer, and preserving long‑tail or rare-token behaviors in NLP.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers behaviors of larger or differently structured models into smaller or alternative models by training students to match teacher outputs, intermediate representations, or other derived supervision signals. Empirically, distillation improves deployment efficiency, can transfer inductive biases and robustness properties, and enables compression across domains including classification, generation, speech, and transformers. Success depends on choices such as what to transfer (logits, features, attention, or synthetic labels), how to combine hard and soft targets, privacy/robustness constraints, and whether teachers are perfect. Contemporary work links distillation to regularization and label smoothing, proposes layer-level and adversarial methods, and demonstrates broad applicability while highlighting limitations tied to teacher quality, data distribution, and adversarial vulnerability.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compressing and Deploying Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible technique that enables transferring predictive power from large models into smaller or more efficient ones. When combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, task-aware selection of distilled signals, quantization-aware training, and privacy-preserving or federated protocols, KD can make state-of-the-art models practically usable on resource-constrained and heterogeneous devices. However, realizing these gains requires attention to what is distilled (outputs versus internal representations), how distilled signals are selected for the target task, and whether data-privacy or communication constraints demand synthetic or distributed distillation procedures.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, low‑risk starting point for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. Treated as a system‑level primitive — selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, combining with complementary compression methods, and adopting data‑aware strategies — KD routinely yields favorable accuracy‑efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a panacea: its practical application requires explicit handling of teacher errors, limited or absent data, distribution shift, and fairness/privacy considerations through targeted mitigations and integrated pipeline design.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical paradigm for compressing and accelerating large deep models by transferring information from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. Across modalities and tasks—supervised classification, representation learning, structured prediction, and generation—research shows KD can produce lightweight models that approach teacher performance, recover performance of small architectures, or enable new deployment constraints (privacy, federated settings). However, success depends critically on what is distilled (outputs, intermediate representations, attention across layers), the data or metadata available for distillation, and the learning dynamics between teacher and student. Open challenges include optimization barriers that prevent exact teacher matching, sensitivity to data heterogeneity, and designing teachers or distillation procedures that reliably transfer the right kind of knowledge for a target student capacity and deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The field encompasses logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, multi-teacher and online regimes, data-free or privacy-aware variants, and architecture-aware pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or automated architecture search. Empirical evidence shows KD commonly recovers most of a teacher’s performance while delivering substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and energy, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, and available data. Open problems remain around domain shift, preserving fine-grained behaviors (e.g., rare tokens), robustness, and principled data-free or privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. Methods extend beyond simple soft-target (logit) matching to include alignment of intermediate representations, attention maps, relational structure, and architecture-aware adaptations. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data‑free approaches), and training curricula (annealing, multi-teacher or online schedules). Empirical work across vision and language shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and design choices that affect robustness, fairness, and generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and System-Level Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive power and support deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, available data, and complementary compression techniques. A pragmatic stance treats KD as the central first-line tool in a broader compression pipeline, combined with pre-training of compact architectures, representation alignment, and targeted interventions for robustness, fairness, and data-limited or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Collier
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically supported approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware design, and deployment-aware data protocols, KD recovers much of teacher performance while enabling real‑world constraints such as latency, memory, and device heterogeneity to be satisfied. KD should be treated as the first‑line method in compression pipelines, but practitioners must co‑design student capacity, distillation signals, and data strategies to mitigate known failure modes such as domain shift, data scarcity, privacy risk, and preservation of rare or fine‑grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably yields compact models that retain much of a larger teacher’s performance when applied with attention to what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability. KD works through multiple mechanisms—soft-target regularization, representation transfer, and ensemble-derived ‘‘dark knowledge’’—and its strengths are maximized when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware training curricula. However, KD is not a universal solution: practical deployments must address limits including distribution shift, rare-token behavior, privacy-sensitive or data-free scenarios, and potential transfer of undesirable teacher behavior. I therefore argue that KD should be treated as the practical core of hybrid compression pipelines, selected and tuned according to deployment constraints and supplemented with methods that mitigate its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression: Effectiveness, Mechanisms, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable strategy to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD succeeds best when treated as a system-level primitive—co-designed with student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search)—and when practitioners use representation-aware objectives, careful layer alignment, and data-aware curricula. KD has clear empirical benefits across vision and NLP but also predictable limits: mismatched teacher–student capacity, scarce or altered data, and long‑tail or rare-token behaviors can reduce transfer quality. Practical deployments therefore require targeted interventions (e.g., projector layers, multi-signal transfer, synthesized data, and robustness checks) to realize reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade a diverse family of distillation methods has emerged—logit-level soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, multi-teacher ensembles, and privacy-aware adaptations—applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative models. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data availability and domain mismatch; combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture search, quantization) and task-aware pipelines yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are a widely adopted toolkit for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers. Research across vision and language characterizes KD as a family of methods—transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training signals via specialized curricula or online exchanges—and shows that KD integrates naturally with pretraining, architecture design, and deployment-aware strategies. Practical success depends on matching the choice of knowledge (what to transfer), the teacher-student pairing (capacity and architecture), available data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and optimization curricula to the target task and constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial runtime and memory gains with modest accuracy loss, open challenges remain in handling domain shift, rare-token transfer in NLP, optimization mismatch, and large-scale or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, But Not Lone, Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible, and empirically effective approach for turning large neural teachers into compact, deployable students. When designed to transfer the right kinds of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, or relational cues), and combined with student-aware architecture choices, data strategies, and privacy-aware procedures, KD yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision, speech, and language tasks. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and deliberate protocol design. Treating KD as a system-level primitive—selected and tuned for task, data, and deployment constraints—produces the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First-Line Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, ensemble consensus), and by combining distillation with data strategies and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: careful selection of distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and evaluation under realistic distribution shifts are necessary to avoid failure modes. Treated as a system-level pipeline rather than a single loss, KD is the recommended first-line strategy for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. When applied as part of a system-level compression pipeline that co-designs student architectures, distillation objectives, and data strategies, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. Effective use of KD requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, available data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or federated protocols). Despite strong empirical results across modalities, open challenges persist in robustness, rare-token behavior, privacy, and theoretical understanding, motivating careful evaluation and targeted remedies in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When combined with architecture-aware design, multi-stage training, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for latency-, memory-, and device-constrained deployments. However, KD’s effectiveness is context-dependent: success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relational signals), teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or synthetic strategies), and operational constraints such as federated heterogeneity and privacy. Practitioners should treat KD as a central tool but evaluate and adapt its signals, data strategy, and integration with other compression techniques to their target deployment scenario.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD operates at multiple levels — softened output distributions, intermediate features and attention maps, relational or contrastive objectives, and module-level behavior — and is often combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (data-free synthesis, public transfer sets). When designed with attention to teacher–student capacity, alignment of representations, and data availability, KD frequently yields compact models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, and ensuring robust, privacy-aware transfer under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictions, internal representations, or relational structure from teacher models. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, distillation methods—ranging from logit-level soft-target matching to feature- and layer-wise alignment, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, self-distillation, and data-free variants—have enabled large reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, availability and quality of data (or synthetic surrogates), and choices about which signals to transfer. Practical pipelines combine distillation with student pre-training, adaptive layer mapping, data augmentation or synthesis, and curriculum schedules; remaining challenges include robustly handling domain shift, preserving low-frequency lexical and fine-grained details, principled teacher selection, and guarantees under privacy or data-limited regimes.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, practitioners use softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, attention- or relation-level signals, multi-teacher and online schedules, and self-distillation. Distillation is typically combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with data strategies that range from using distilled teacher outputs to synthetic or data-free approaches. Empirical successes include large reductions in inference cost while preserving most of the teacher’s performance, but failures arise when teacher–student misalignment, data mismatch, low-frequency outputs, or privacy constraints are not addressed. Practical pipelines treat distillation as a flexible, context-aware toolkit rather than a fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a simple teacher-student training recipe into a multifaceted toolkit that enables efficient, robust, and privacy-aware deployment of deep models. KD not only compresses large models into faster, smaller students suitable for edge and production, but also enables task-adaptive compression, data-limited or data-free scenarios, privacy-preserving federated setups, and transfers of inductive biases across architectures. When combined with complementary techniques such as architecture search, specialized feature-matching losses, and careful input-side interventions, KD yields practical compressed models without prohibitive losses in accuracy and can improve generalization in out-of-distribution settings.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The approach spans logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but its empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and training dynamics; open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, robustness, privacy, and heterogeneous architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple softened-target matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online regimes, adversarial decision-boundary techniques, and data-aware or data-free strategies. When integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility and data provenance, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Important limitations remain, including sensitivity to distribution shift, data- and privacy-constrained settings, preserving long-tail behaviors, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher biases; addressing these issues requires pipeline-oriented, context-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When integrated with task-aware student design, data or augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD reliably reduces memory, compute, and latency while preserving—or sometimes improving—accuracy and specific properties (e.g., robustness or multimodal capabilities). This paper argues that KD should be treated as the primary, adaptable instrument in model-compression toolkits for practical deep-learning and NLP systems, and outlines concrete mechanisms and caveats for its application.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and inference cost across vision and language tasks. When treated as a flexible toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level supervision, multi-teacher schedules, data- or privacy-aware synthesis, and integration with pruning/quantization/search—KD supports practical deployment under latency, memory, and data constraints. However, realizing its full potential requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to data availability (including data-free and zero-shot approaches), and task- or architecture-aware objectives to avoid optimization and distributional failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Crawford
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher‑student recipe into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and explicitly addressing robustness and distributional shifts. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, training regimes, practical recommendations, and remaining challenges for KD-driven model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Ramsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically grounded approach for transferring the behavior of large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a system-level primitive rather than a single loss, KD can provide multiple types of supervisory signals, interface with complementary compression methods, and be shaped by data- and deployment-aware choices. Adopting KD as a first‑line strategy enables strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs in many realistic settings, provided practitioners explicitly address teacher–student compatibility, data provenance, and known risks such as distribution shift, rare-token degradation, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD reduces inference cost and memory while often retaining much of teacher performance. KD manifests in many forms — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relation- or token-level signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation variants, and data-aware or data-free protocols — and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable distillation data, careful choice of distillation signals and schedules, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and privacy; remaining challenges include preserving rare-token behavior, coping with distribution shift, and preventing transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller or otherwise constrained models. Approaches span from matching outputs to mimicking intermediate representations, from layer-aware mapping strategies to task-adaptive architecture search, and include protocols for heterogeneous, data-constrained, or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical results across vision and language tasks demonstrate strong gains in efficiency with modest drops (or even improvements) in performance, while persistent challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, choosing appropriate sources of knowledge, and designing robust data-free or federated distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Extensions, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable method for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely yields favorable trade‑offs of accuracy, latency, and memory across speech, vision, and language tasks. However, its success depends on data availability, teacher quality, and deployment constraints; effective use treats KD as the first line of a broader, context‑aware compression pipeline rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all solution.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher→student soft-label transfer into a broad toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across vision, language, and multimodal domains. Contemporary approaches extend logits matching to representation- and structure-aware objectives, multi- and continual-teaching schemes, task-aware layer selection, and combinations with pruning or architecture-level compression. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints but its success depends on design choices about what is transferred, how the student is supervised, data availability, and student capacity. Practical progress emphasizes representation matching beyond logits, careful layer- and channel-level alignment, and composing KD with other compression techniques; remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, data-free scenarios, and preserving fine-grained or safety-critical behavior.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely used approach to compressing large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods span soft-logit matching, ensemble distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and privacy- or data-aware variants. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show that carefully chosen distillation targets and student–teacher alignment can achieve large reductions in inference cost with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in performance. However, practical success depends on capacity-matching, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, degraded rare-token behavior in NLP, and privacy concerns. KD performs best as a component of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture choices, pruning/quantization, and data-centric strategies.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces inference cost by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller student models. The field has evolved from simple soft‑label matching to a rich set of techniques that transfer logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and that integrate with architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data strategies. Practical deployments rely on matching the form of distilled knowledge to student capacity and task constraints, using pre‑training or task‑aware adaptation when possible, and addressing optimization and data limitations. Remaining challenges include data‑free distillation, robustness and fairness under compression, domain shift, and principled choices for heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A rich set of distillation techniques—including soft-target/logit matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, adversarial and relational objectives, multi-teacher schemes, and data-synthesis or data-free approaches—has been applied across NLP, vision, graphs, ranking, and healthcare. Practical compression usually pairs distillation with architecture-aware strategies (pruning, quantization, or search) and careful design choices about what, how, and when to transfer knowledge; success depends on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and attention to robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact students. Distillation strategies include transferring softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, distilling relational or task‑specific signals, and applying progressive or self‑distillation schedules. In practice KD is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that considers student architecture, data availability, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Remaining challenges center on data‑poor or data‑free settings, preserving rare or safety‑critical behaviors, avoiding blind transfer of biases, and developing stronger theory to predict when and how distillation succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. Across vision and NLP, KD methods extend beyond logit matching to include intermediate-representation imitation, attention and relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-constrained or data-free procedures. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines—especially when combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, or quantization—regularly yield compact models that recover much of the teacher’s performance, though open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, fairness, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models. When designed with attention to what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), how teacher and student are aligned, and the data available for training, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD also integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapts to specialized settings such as multi-teacher ensembles, heterogeneous-device deployments, generative-model compression, low-precision inference, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited environments. However, KD is not uniformly automatic: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, distributional match, and design of distillation objectives and curricula.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around what to transfer (outputs, features, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, and the realities of data and deployment, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, distillation is context-dependent: its success requires complementary compression methods, careful handling of data- and privacy-constraints, and explicit evaluation for robustness and rare or safety-critical behaviors. Treated as the central component of a broader compression pipeline—rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe—KD enables reliable, production-ready model compression across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces the cost of deploying large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models. A diverse set of KD variants—soft-target matching, internal-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance, online and meta-learned teaching, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches—enable tradeoffs among size, latency, and retained performance. Practical deployments commonly combine KD with architecture-aware transformations (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign), data-management strategies, and training schedules to address constraints such as limited data, device heterogeneity, privacy, and fairness. While KD often produces strong empirical gains, its success depends on careful choices about what and how to transfer, student capacity and architecture, and the provenance of training data; persistent challenges include domain shift, teacher errors, preserving rare behaviors, and avoiding unintentional transfer of bias.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students that retain much of the teacher's performance. Across NLP, vision, and generative models, KD takes many forms (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free synthesis) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving accuracy under many conditions, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and optimization protocols. Practical deployment requires careful design choices and remains an active area for research on robustness, rare-token preservation, privacy, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Lindsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Pipeline Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining predictive performance. KD methods include soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate representation and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free strategies. In practice KV succeeds when integrated into compression pipelines that also consider student architecture, pruning/quantization, data strategies, and explicit evaluations for robustness and rare-case behavior. However, KD has contextual limits driven by teacher–student mismatch, data availability or privacy constraints, optimization dynamics, and distribution shift; addressing these requires targeted design choices, careful signal selection, and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, attention/relational signals, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or synthesized-data variants—that often recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what and how to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior. KD therefore functions best as a central component within a broader compression and deployment pipeline rather than as a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.
