papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compress large deep models and transfer knowledge to smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. Across vision and language applications, KD encompasses teacher-student paradigms that use teacher soft targets, intermediate representations, or auxiliary objectives; extensions include multi-teacher setups, data-free distillation, meta-learned teachers, and device-aware distillation for heterogeneous deployments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in parameters and inference cost; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and how dataset complexity, teacher quality, and student capacity interact to determine outcomes. Practical strategies combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques to meet deployment constraints while retaining generalization.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match the right form of teacher knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational or contrastive signals) and combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and targeted objectives; therefore KD should be treated as a first-line tool that must be adapted to the deployment context rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Matthews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels — soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational constraints, or ensemble targets — and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware redesign). Empirically, distilled students frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability (including data-free or privacy-sensitive regimes), and training protocols; important open problems remain in robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare-token or safety-critical behaviors, and principled design of distillation objectives.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational alignment—consistently enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while recovering much of teacher accuracy when applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization dynamics. Practical KD pipelines typically combine distilled signals with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adopt data-aware strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols) to address real-world deployment challenges. Key open problems include robustly preserving long-tail or rare behaviors, handling distribution shift and privacy constraints, and automating student design for strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across deep learning and NLP, KD methods span soft-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, online and adversarial schemes, and data‑constrained or data‑free protocols. KD is most effective when co‑designed with student architectures, appropriate data strategies, and complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization). However, its success is context dependent: teacher quality and compatibility, data provenance and availability, distribution shift, and the need to preserve rare or safety‑critical behaviors constrain outcomes. Understanding KD’s mechanisms, choosing suitable transfer signals, and integrating complementary methods are key to reliable, practical compression.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses multiple transfer targets (softened logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), operational modes (offline, online, self- or multi-teacher), and data strategies (real, augmented, synthetic, or data-free). When integrated with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware redesign, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for vision, speech, and language tasks. Its practical success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, and the provenance and match of training data materially influence outcomes. Remaining gaps include principled theory of when distillation helps, reliable transfer of robustness and fairness, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, and automating student-objective selection for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has been adapted beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature supervision, layer- or module-level mapping, selective sample transfer, data-free synthesis, and combinations with other compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments reveal important dependencies on teacher quality, student architecture, data availability, and training protocols; when these are handled deliberately, distilled models can achieve strong trade-offs in accuracy, latency, and resource use. Remaining challenges include robust transfer under data heterogeneity, preserving low-frequency or rare outputs, and aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures in privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Brooks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Contexts, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD methods include soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-representation and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free variants. When KD is co-designed with student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), it routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD’s effectiveness is context-dependent: success requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, availability and provenance of data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distributional-shift risks. Treating KD as a central, system-level tool—rather than a single recipe—maximizes its practical benefits while making its limitations manageable.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that students can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Methods extend beyond matching softened logits to include intermediate representation and attention matching, relational or contrastive objectives, ensemble-to-single schedules, online or co‑distillation, and data‑aware or data‑free variants. In practice, KD is most effective when its signals are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints, and when it is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic data). Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or fine‑grained behavior (especially in NLP), aligning heterogeneous architectures, and maintaining robustness, fairness, and privacy under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong empirical gains in memory and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance, and it naturally extends beyond logits to include intermediate representations, attention maps, and synthesized inputs. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and transfer of unwanted behaviors mean distillation must be treated as a design pattern within a broader compression pipeline. When combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary techniques such as pruning and quantization, KD reliably supports real-world deployment while demanding careful, task-aware choices to avoid failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Powerful but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Its effectiveness arises from the ability to transfer different forms of knowledge (soft labels, intermediate features, attention, ensembles) and to combine distillation with data augmentation, pretraining, and task-aware objectives. However, KD is not uniformly successful: outcomes depend on teacher-student capacity alignment, the choice of distillation targets, data availability and augmentation strategy, and deployment constraints such as privacy or device heterogeneity. Careful selection of distillation signals, task-aware layer matching, and augmentation or synthetic-data strategies improve robustness; conversely, mismatches in architecture, domain shift, or heterogeneous federated settings can sharply limit benefits.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Outcomes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Approaches vary from matching final soft targets to transferring intermediate representations, leveraging ensembles or multiple teachers, to data-free synthesis and combining KD with pruning or low-precision numerics. In NLP, KD has enabled compact models to approach the performance of large pre-trained models while substantially reducing inference cost. Recent work clarifies theoretical mechanisms, proposes many-to-many layer alignment techniques, and develops adaptive multi-teacher weighting and zero-shot distillation to broaden applicability. Despite strong empirical gains, open challenges remain in task-specific alignment, robustness to heterogeneous data, and preserving fairness and calibration during compression.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system-level design primitive—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression and data strategies—it routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Responsible application requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance (including data-free options), and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans algorithmic advances in teacher–student objectives, architecture-aware compression, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Practical work shows gains from combining KD with data augmentation, many-to-many layer mappings, and architecture search, while complementary efforts address data-free and privacy-preserving distillation. Remaining challenges include imperfect teachers, data heterogeneity, and adapting compression to task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure through a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and supports variants such as multi-teacher, online, adversarial, and data-free distillation. Its effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, what and how knowledge is transferred, data availability (or synthetic data strategies), and complementary compression mechanisms (architecture search, pruning, quantization). While KD has enabled many real-world deployments across modalities, its limits include sensitivity to distribution shift, optimization mismatches, fairness and privacy concerns, and challenges in aligning heterogeneous architectures. Best practice treats KD as a core first-line strategy combined with targeted methods tailored to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become practical tools to reduce model size and computation while retaining much of the performance of large teachers. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, approaches include transferring soft logits, mimicking internal features or attention maps, layering/structural adaptations, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-preserving methods. Empirical results demonstrate that careful distillation can yield compact students that approach teacher accuracy and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, but open challenges remain in robustness, task-specific distillation design, and distributed training dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, Results, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened logits to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schedules, data‑free and synthetic-data strategies, and teacher-training schemes that improve transfer. When combined with architecture-aware redesign, pruning, and quantization, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. However, practical success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals with student capacity, appropriate data strategies, and evaluation for robustness, long-tail behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD should be treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is chosen and tuned to match teacher–student capacity, data availability, deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy), and architectural heterogeneity. When designed with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), projector or alignment modules, and complementary compression techniques, distillation reliably enables compact, efficient models for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications. However, careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and domain shift is required to avoid failure modes and degraded behavior.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable design paradigm—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely achieves strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher quality, and evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints; practitioners should therefore apply KD together with targeted validation, robustness checks, and complementary engineering such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, practitioners use softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, attention- or relation-level signals, multi-teacher and online schedules, and self-distillation. Distillation is typically combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with data strategies that range from using distilled teacher outputs to synthetic or data-free approaches. Empirical successes include large reductions in inference cost while preserving most of the teacher’s performance, but failures arise when teacher–student misalignment, data mismatch, low-frequency outputs, or privacy constraints are not addressed. Practical pipelines treat distillation as a flexible, context-aware toolkit rather than a fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Effective and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Risks, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of large, high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. KD delivers large gains in inference speed and memory while preserving much of the teacher's utility across NLP tasks (including question answering and sentence understanding) and other modalities. However, naive distillation can transfer undesirable properties such as bias, privacy leakage, or fragility to distribution shift and adversarial attacks. A combination of strategies—student-aware teacher design, multi-teacher curricula, selective sample distillation, data augmentation, adversarial and robust distillation, and privacy-aware ensembles—provides a pragmatic path to compress models while controlling fairness, robustness, and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, versatile approach for shrinking large models into compact students that are deployable under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. Its success depends on treating distillation not as a single loss but as a system design choice: selecting what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relations), how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, what data or synthetic surrogates to use, and which complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to combine. KD delivers substantial efficiency gains in many settings but is context-dependent: careful choices about teacher quality, data availability, and objective design are required to avoid failure modes such as capacity mismatch, degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena, or privacy/robustness tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Landry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broadly applicable, practical approach for shrinking large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD encompasses logit/soft-target transfer, intermediate-representation and attention matching, and online or multi-teacher variants; when combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and care about data and optimization, KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability, pretraining, and robustness and fairness constraints, so it functions best as a central component within a larger, deployment‑aware compression pipeline rather than as a single universal recipe.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, retrieval, visual recognition, graph-based prediction, and data-limited or privacy-constrained settings—distillation enables latency- and resource-constrained deployment. However, straightforward distillation is not a panacea: distribution shifts, heterogeneity of data and models, and absence of training data expose weaknesses that require complementary techniques (e.g., internal representation matching, layer mapping, task-aware selection, generative replay). Combining these advances yields compressed models that are both accurate and robust for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and pragmatic framework for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or more private models across modalities and tasks. When applied thoughtfully — by matching outputs, intermediate representations, training dynamics, or ensembles — KD can preserve or even improve task performance while enabling low-latency inference, reduced memory/compute, and new deployment modes (e.g., federated, data-free, or low-precision). However, distillation is not automatic: design choices about what to transfer, when to transfer, and how to align teacher and student matter for robustness, domain shifts, and rare-token behavior. I argue that best practice combines representation-aware objectives, selective or collaborative teaching strategies, and deployment-aware constraints (privacy, communication, numeric precision) to realize the full benefits of distillation in NLP and other deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique that transfers richer supervision from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention and relation matching, and multi‑teacher or self‑distillation schedules; when combined with data strategies and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) it routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, optimization choices, and targeted evaluation for robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behaviors. Best practice treats KD as the core of an integrated compression pipeline, adapted to task and deployment constraints and explicitly designed to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central to deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained settings. The literature spans theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps, practical algorithms for distilling logits, representations, and attention, techniques that require no original data, and adaptations for domains such as NLP, machine translation, and distributed training. Empirical work has shown KD can both accelerate inference and enable smaller models to approach or even exceed teacher performance in some settings, while recent advances address domain adaptivity, robustness, and teacher–student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features, attention patterns, and relational signals, and they are frequently combined with structural compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and recommendation tasks shows KD can produce compact models with strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of transferred signals, data availability (including data-free or few-shot scenarios), and careful optimization and evaluation. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a toolkit that must be tailored to task, data, and system constraints and augmented with diagnostics for robustness, fairness, and rare-token or out-of-distribution behavior.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When treated as a system‑level design primitive and combined with complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across modalities. Its success depends on careful choices of distilled signals, teacher–student co‑design, data and augmentation strategies, and targeted evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy. Responsible deployment treats KD as the default first step for compression while explicitly addressing its limitations and integrating additional methods where needed.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Sparks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone and can be adapted to diverse constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Its practical success relies on careful co‑design of teacher and student, selection of what knowledge to transfer, data strategies (including privacy‑preserving or data‑free variants), and combination with complementary compression methods. KD is best treated as a central element of compression pipelines rather than a standalone cure: when integrated with architecture-aware compression and rigorous evaluation under deployment conditions, it yields compact models that preserve much of teacher behavior while respecting resource and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. When treated as a system-level primitive rather than a single loss term, KD can be adapted to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch to produce compact models that retain much of teachers' performance. Practical application of KD involves choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to expose students to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online predictions), and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods and privacy-preserving protocols. Despite strong empirical success, KD has known failure modes tied to teacher errors, limited data, and distribution shift that require targeted mitigations and principled design.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models so as to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has diversified from matching softened output distributions to a toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and synthetic-data approaches). KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when data and evaluation practices account for domain shift, robustness, and rare-class behaviours. Important open problems remain around principled transfer across heterogeneous architectures, preserving safety-critical or long-tail behavior, data‑free and privacy‑respecting distillation, and understanding what exactly is transferred from teacher to student.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and distributed settings KD often recovers much of a teacher's predictive performance while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and deployment under resource or privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: outcomes depend on what signals are transferred (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, availability and quality of data (including data-free or federated setups), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats distillation as one element of a compression pipeline that combines representation matching, architecture-aware student design, data strategies, and risk-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolkit—ranging from softened-output matching to representation-level imitation and multi-teacher or data-free variants—that integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on principled teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it is a flexible, multi-signal toolkit that preserves much of a teacher’s performance while enabling large gains in latency, memory, and deployability. KD combines naturally with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). Its reliable use requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate and mitigate risks such as degraded long-tail behavior, robustness failures, and privacy leakage.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD succeeds across modalities when treated as a design pipeline that combines what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints and deployment constraints (privacy, latency, heterogeneity). KD is powerful but not universally sufficient: realizing its benefits requires co-design of teacher and student, complementary compression techniques, and safeguards for low-frequency phenomena, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A diverse set of KD mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data synthesis—has been developed and combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many vision and language tasks, while remaining sensitive to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, domain shift, and robustness concerns. Practical pipelines therefore co-design student architectures, distillation targets, and data handling strategies to achieve the best trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and other modalities. A broad family of techniques transfers different forms of teacher information — from softened logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data-free synthesis and adversarially guided generation). Empirical evidence shows that, when carefully designed to match teacher–student capacity and data conditions, KD can retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, mitigating bias transfer, and characterizing when particular distillation objectives succeed in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Targeted Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior from larger teacher models into smaller students. The field has evolved beyond matching softened output logits to include representation-level guidance, attention and relational targets, data-augmentation and synthesis strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision and language shows that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while reducing compute, memory, and latency; however, success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and provenance, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as one component of a compression toolkit, integrating architecture choices, precision reductions, and data strategies to meet production constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teachers. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer schemes that mimic intermediate representations, attention, or relational signals, and it can be combined with pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture search. Practical effectiveness depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity, managing limited or private data, and choosing inputs and objectives that preserve fine-grained behaviors. The following synthesis summarizes prevailing mechanisms, representative techniques, empirical strengths and failure modes, and practical recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD supports domain adaptation, latency-aware architecture transformations, robustness transfer, and interpretable model surrogates. When combined with careful training protocols (e.g., multi-teacher schemes, domain adaptation, or targeted regularization), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models in resource- and latency-constrained or safety-critical settings across vision, speech, 3D perception, and natural language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, privacy) while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive power. KD has grown from soft-label (logit) matching into a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer alignment, relational and contrastive signals, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. In practice KD is most effective when signals, student architecture, and data strategies are co-designed for the target task and deployment context and when KD is combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include theoretical understanding, robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors in language tasks, and distillation under data-scarce or privacy-sensitive constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field has matured into a suite of complementary techniques — logits matching, feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher schedules, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search — and is applied across NLP, vision, speech, multimodal, and specialized domains. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover most teacher performance and enable deployment under strict compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on adapting objectives, data strategies, and student architectures to task and deployment constraints. Key open problems include distillation under data heterogeneity and privacy, preserving rare-token fidelity for sequence tasks, transferring robustness, and automating student architectures for diverse tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods transfer information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, cheaper models to reduce inference cost while retaining accuracy. Across computer vision, speech, recommender systems and natural language processing, KD variants have targeted soft-label transfer, relational or feature imitation, self-distillation, and teacher adaptation to improve student generalization. Practical work emphasizes complementary strategies — pretraining compact architectures, specialist teacher training, careful input augmentation, and training-time efficiency — to address optimization mismatch, domain shift, and computational overhead. Remaining challenges include imperfect matching between teacher and student distributions, choosing data and augmentation strategies that preserve useful teacher signals, and designing distillation procedures that scale to constrained hardware and domain-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field has developed a broad toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and feature-level transfer, multi‑teacher and online schemes, and data‑free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data strategies, and optimization choices are carefully managed. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, handling teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and fairness under compression, and operating under limited or no access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Burgess
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals from larger teacher models to smaller students. The KD toolkit spans softened-output (logit) supervision, representation- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and online or multi-teacher schedules; it interoperates with structural compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When KD is co‑designed with student architectures and appropriate data strategies, it routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but its success depends on teacher quality, data availability (or synthesis), capacity and architecture mismatch, and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token or long‑tail behaviors, and privacy-sensitive constraints. Outstanding research directions include principled teacher selection and adaptation, reliable data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, faithful transfer of robustness and rare-token performance in language models, and scalable distributed or online distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep-learning models into smaller, deployable students. When designed and applied carefully, KD reduces inference latency, memory footprint, and deployment cost while preserving much of a teacher model’s performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what information is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Treating KD as a design paradigm—co-designing teachers and students, selecting appropriate distillation signals, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—yields the most reliable path to efficient models in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context‑Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied deliberately—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and inputs, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely delivers large reductions in model size and latency while preserving most task performance. Real-world success requires representation-aware objectives, options for data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, and careful evaluation under distribution shift and modality-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger, often more expensive teacher models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Research over the past decade has developed a spectrum of KD objectives (soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, contrastive and relational losses), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online co-training, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules), and deployment-aware integrations (pre-training students, architecture-aware adapters, and combination with pruning or quantization). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while reducing parameter count and latency, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and the choice of what and how to transfer. Ongoing challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, matching heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency or domain-specific signals, and automating trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically effective paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and combining distillation with other compression tools—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of the original model's performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on capacity matching, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and optimization design. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a central tool to be combined with architecture-aware choices and task-specific adjustments to meet real deployment constraints.
