papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses multiple transfer targets (softened logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), operational modes (offline, online, self- or multi-teacher), and data strategies (real, augmented, synthetic, or data-free). When integrated with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware redesign, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for vision, speech, and language tasks. Its practical success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, and the provenance and match of training data materially influence outcomes. Remaining gaps include principled theory of when distillation helps, reliable transfer of robustness and fairness, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, and automating student-objective selection for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and compression seek to retain performance of large deep models while reducing size and latency for deployment. Methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include transferring internal representations, attention maps, and relational or adversarial signals; they can be applied during pretraining, task fine-tuning, or domain adaptation, and may operate with or without access to original training data. Empirical results across retrieval, reading comprehension, pretrained language models, and other domains show consistent trade-offs where careful choice of distillation targets, training curricula, and data augmentation materially improves student generalization and robustness while substantially lowering compute and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language tasks. KD delivers compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and adaptations for data- or privacy-constrained settings. Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits, representations, attention maps), how to align teacher and student, and which data strategies and curricula to use. KD should therefore be treated as a first-line, system-level strategy in compression pipelines, but applied with explicit attention to context, complementary techniques, and evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted paradigm for producing smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into compact students. Across vision, generation, and natural language tasks, KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and adversarial-data strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods. Empirical practice shows KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when teacher–student design, choice of distillation signal, and data strategies are co‑designed for the target deployment, but persistent challenges remain in domain shift, privacy-constrained and data-limited settings, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language processing. A range of techniques—transferring soft logits, mimicking internal features or attention maps, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or zero-shot approaches—enable tradeoffs between model size, latency, and retained performance. Distillation is applied not only for inference efficiency but also for domain adaptation, privacy-preserving federated training, and task-specific transfer. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student design, data considerations, and optimization strategies; ongoing challenges include robustness under domain shift, imperfect teachers, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Constraints, and Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models or otherwise reduce model size while retaining performance. Core approaches include matching teacher soft-targets, aligning intermediate representations (features, attention), and combining distillation with structural compression (pruning, quantization) or automated architecture design. Practical uses span on-device deployment, task-adaptive compression, lifelong and continual learning, robustness preservation, and privacy-aware or data-free scenarios. Success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (or synthesis), and training protocols; addressing these factors via complementary strategies yields the best accuracy–efficiency trade-offs while exposing open challenges in robustness, fairness, and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compress large neural models into smaller, more deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Contemporary work shows KD is not a single algorithm but a family of techniques that transfer knowledge via soft labels, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise mappings, data augmentation, and even data-free synthesis. KD has been applied across modalities and tasks — from compressing large language and multimodal transformers to enabling lightweight generative models and resource-efficient inference on edge devices. Empirical and theoretical analyses have begun to explain when and why distillation works, how it transfers inductive biases, and which input-side interventions (e.g., mixup/CutMix variants) improve transfer. Practical challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and deciding what form of teacher knowledge (logits, features, relations, or structural priors) best serves a given student architecture.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably yields compact models that retain much of a larger teacher’s performance when applied with attention to what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability. KD works through multiple mechanisms—soft-target regularization, representation transfer, and ensemble-derived ‘‘dark knowledge’’—and its strengths are maximized when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware training curricula. However, KD is not a universal solution: practical deployments must address limits including distribution shift, rare-token behavior, privacy-sensitive or data-free scenarios, and potential transfer of undesirable teacher behavior. I therefore argue that KD should be treated as the practical core of hybrid compression pipelines, selected and tuned according to deployment constraints and supplemented with methods that mitigate its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from one or more high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relation-aware losses, layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained transformers, self-distillation, curriculum-driven distillation, and complementary use with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and enables deployment under stringent latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining as much task performance as possible. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a broad set of practical techniques that include intermediate representation matching, layer-wise alignment, online and multi-teacher training, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can substantially shrink model size and latency for vision and language systems and can be adapted for privacy-sensitive and distributed settings; however, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and the availability or synthesis of suitable training data, and it faces open challenges in robustness, cross-domain generalization, and heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical toolkit for turning large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Methods vary from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, latency, and energy, but success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, optimization choices, and targeted handling of robustness, low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive settings. Important open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, preserving rare-token and domain-specific signals, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers or data are scarce, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large or ensemble models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad set of mechanisms — including softened logits, representation-level imitation, attention/relational alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data‑constrained protocols — are used in practice. Empirical work shows well-designed distillation pipelines often recover most teacher performance while enabling large reductions in latency and memory, but deployment requires careful attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, privacy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD should be treated as a first‑line strategy: it reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with capacity-aware student design, appropriate distilled signals, and complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure — its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability and provenance, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks — so practitioners must apply KD as part of an integrated compression pipeline and evaluate its trade-offs in realistic deployment settings.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational alignment—consistently enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while recovering much of teacher accuracy when applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization dynamics. Practical KD pipelines typically combine distilled signals with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adopt data-aware strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols) to address real-world deployment challenges. Key open problems include robustly preserving long-tail or rare behaviors, handling distribution shift and privacy constraints, and automating student design for strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under resource constraints. Rather than a single algorithm, KD comprises multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) that should be chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and downstream requirements. Effective compression usually combines KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization) and careful alignment between teacher and student. Practical success thus depends on design choices and trade-offs rather than a universal distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a system-level technique—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints—KD routinely produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines combine diverse signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), and complementary compression steps (progressive module replacement, pruning, quantization) to address domain shifts and deployment constraints. Despite limitations related to teacher–student mismatch and optimization challenges, KD's adaptability across tasks and ability to incorporate robustness and data-free methods make it the recommended primary approach for real-world model compression.

A rich set of distillation techniques—including soft-target/logit matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, adversarial and relational objectives, multi-teacher schemes, and data-synthesis or data-free approaches—has been applied across NLP, vision, graphs, ranking, and healthcare. Practical compression usually pairs distillation with architecture-aware strategies (pruning, quantization, or search) and careful design choices about what, how, and when to transfer knowledge; success depends on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and attention to robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of objectives and training regimes—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, attention/relational signals, data- or privacy-aware synthesis, and teacher–student co-design—that together enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, available data, teacher/student compatibility, and complementary compression techniques; open challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, distillation without original data, and principled handling of heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Barrett
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated set of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, multimodal and domain-specific tasks, KD methods—ranging from softened-logit matching to intermediate feature, attention and relational transfers—are typically combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). Empirically, KD frequently produces students that recover much of teacher performance and improve deployment efficiency, but practical success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, choice of distillation signals, data availability, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, rare-token/long-tail behavior, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. A broad family of approaches—from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols—enables deployment across vision, speech, and language tasks. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signal to student capacity, combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining), and addressing data, optimization, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable framework for producing compact models by transferring behavior from larger teachers to smaller students. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource constraints, and it extends beyond simple logit matching to include feature-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its efficacy depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled information, data availability, capacity mismatch, and fairness or robustness concerns. A considered KD pipeline—combining soft-targets, internal representation guidance, task-aware objectives, and suitable data strategies—yields robust, efficient students fitting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational signals) and are commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design). Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks when distillation signals, student capacity, and data strategies are matched to deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include handling teacher errors and biases, preserving rare or long‑tail behaviors (especially in NLP), and reliably distilling across architecture or domain gaps; practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a toolkit that must be adapted to task, data, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has matured from simple logits-matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes soft-target supervision, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relation matching, data synthesis for data-free scenarios, online and federated distillation, and self-distillation. Empirical results show distilled students often approach teacher performance while yielding substantial gains in latency, memory, and deployability; however, practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as bias transfer, robustness loss, and privacy leakage. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative variants, theoretical insights, practical strategies, and open challenges to guide research and deployments in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, data-free or few-shot protocols). Practical outcomes depend on teacher quality and specialization, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability; open problems include reliable transfer under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and operating under privacy or data-limited constraints.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and adversarially or synthetically generated inputs. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data strategies, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success depends on careful matching of what is transferred to student capacity, handling data scarcity or distribution shift, and mitigating propagation of teacher errors. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, representative algorithmic families, empirical patterns, and actionable recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and natural language processing. When integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Effective application requires deliberate choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle limited or domain-shifted data, and how to audit robustness and rare-token behavior. Treated as a first-line, context-aware tool rather than a one-size-fits-all cure, KD enables practical deployments while highlighting research directions around robustness, privacy, and heterogeneous-architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervision richer than hard labels. A diverse set of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate representations and attention, relational or contrastive objectives, ensemble and online schemes, and data-aware synthesis—combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) yields compact models that often retain most of a teacher’s performance. Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data access and alignment, and optimization choices; remaining challenges include reliable data-free distillation, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, transfer of robustness and fairness properties, and reducing the computational cost of distillation itself.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practically effective approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When KD is applied as a system‑level strategy—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, combining distillation with other compression techniques, and adopting appropriate data strategies—it routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs for vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its outcomes depend on teacher quality, student architecture and capacity, data availability and provenance, and deployment concerns such as robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. Effective practice treats KD as the default first‑line tool within a broader, deployment‑aware compression pipeline rather than as a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural networks for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Beyond simple model-size reduction, KD enables transfer of inductive biases, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving distributed training, data-free and zero-shot compression, and the transfer of adversarial robustness. Combining logit-based distillation with feature-level mimicking and carefully chosen regularization yields high-quality small models that remain competitive on downstream tasks in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically supported path to compress large models into compact, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a central design pattern rather than a single loss term, KD enables multiple transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and online schedules, and integration with architecture-aware design and other compression methods. Practical success requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including pre-training of compact architectures and data augmentation or synthesis), and theoretical understanding of when soft versus hard supervision helps. Framed this way, KD is the most practical, multi-strategy mechanism for real-world compression, provided practitioners pair it with complementary techniques and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) supervision to include intermediate feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, and handling data availability or provenance; open problems include principled teacher design, robust data-free approaches, preserving long-tail or safety-critical behaviors, and theoretical characterization of when particular knowledge sources help.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so the students meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, and privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, using multi- or online-teacher schedules, and employing data-aware or data-free synthesis; it is frequently combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful student design. Empirical practice emphasizes co-design of distillation signals, student capacity and architecture, and data or augmentation strategies, while ongoing challenges include reliable distillation without original data, robust transfer under domain shift, preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, and privacy and fairness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multi‑Strategy Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is most useful when treated as a system-level, context-sensitive toolkit rather than a single loss term. Properly designed distillation pipelines combine multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals), teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, data provenance (including options for data-free distillation), and explicit evaluation of robustness, rare-token fidelity, and fairness. A pragmatic research and engineering agenda focuses on matching distillation signals to student capacity, designing student-friendly teachers, integrating online and multi-teacher regimes where appropriate, and developing reliable data-free or privacy-aware procedures.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Practical Strengths, Limits, and a Pragmatic Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of methods for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Over a range of modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive objectives), and they can be combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or synthetic-data generation) to meet deployment constraints. KD reliably improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when teacher and student are properly aligned and when the distillation strategy matches data and system constraints; however, it is not a universal solution. Key limitations include sensitivity to teacher–student capacity mismatch, degraded transfer on low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena, and challenges when original training data are unavailable or under distribution shift. A pragmatic KD practice chooses appropriate distilled signals, co-designs student architectures, uses synthetic or adversarially generated data when needed, and evaluates robustness and fairness under realistic deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervision richer than hard labels alone. Over the last decade KD evolved from soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes internal-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When co-designed with student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression steps such as pruning and quantization, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs; however, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data provenance, and explicit handling of robustness, long-tail behaviors, and undesirable teacher biases. Practitioners should therefore treat distillation as a central, context-dependent element of an integrated compression pipeline and use targeted diagnostics and mitigation for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary—but Not Sole—Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervision beyond hard labels. KD methods (soft-logit transfer, intermediate-feature matching, attention imitation, ensemble and relational signals, and data‑aware or data‑free schemes) routinely produce strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when they are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints. In production settings KD is most effective when treated as the backbone of a system-level compression pipeline—co-designed with architecture search, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and explicit evaluations for robustness, rare‑token behavior, privacy, and fairness. KD remains limited in scenarios with little or no data, in preserving fine‑grained rare behaviors, and under distribution shift; these limitations motivate hybrid pipelines and targeted remedies rather than abandoning KD as a primary tool.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods have become central tools for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy and capabilities of large teachers. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of techniques—ranging from distilling logits, internal representations, and attention patterns to data-free and few-shot strategies, multi-teacher ensembles, and task-adaptive search for student architectures. These approaches have been applied across vision, language, multimodal, and deployed/distributed settings, demonstrating substantial gains in inference speed and model size while exposing trade-offs in robustness, data requirements, and modality alignment. This survey summarizes the main algorithmic families, common engineering strategies, notable empirical outcomes, and key open challenges for applying distillation in practice.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First‑line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Necessary Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, first‑line compression strategy for deep learning and NLP systems because it offers flexible, task‑aware transfer channels that preserve predictive behavior while enabling complementary structural compression. KD’s strengths—multiple transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational information), compatibility with multi-teacher and data‑synthesis techniques, and composability with pruning/quantization and architecture design—make it the most practical backbone for deployment. However, KD is context‑dependent: its success requires careful teacher–student alignment, attention to data availability (including data‑free or privacy‑constrained regimes), and explicit evaluation for robustness and distribution shift. A KD‑first pipeline that selects appropriate distillation targets, reconciles representational mismatches, and composes KD with structural compression and data strategies yields compact, deployable models while limiting common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving performance. Approaches span soft-label (logit) matching, feature- or attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data-free distillation, and adaptations for domain shift and heterogeneous deployment. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, training curricula, and application-specific design choices. Emerging theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and reveal practical tradeoffs such as bias–variance effects of soft labels and the roles of ensemble and self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques to transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students). Approaches vary from soft-label supervision and internal representation matching to data-free synthesis, task-adaptive architecture search, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show distilled students can approach teacher performance while enabling deployment under computational, storage, privacy, or bandwidth constraints; open challenges include robustness, heterogeneity of data and models, and few-shot or label-scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Villa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple channels of transferable information (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals) and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design). I argue KD should be treated as the backbone of compression pipelines: used by default as a first‑line strategy but applied in a context‑aware way, co‑designed with student architectures and data regimes, and paired with explicit mitigations for known failure modes such as distribution shift, rare-token degradation, privacy leakage, and teacher bias.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, pragmatic approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD has diversified from soft‑target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate‑representation and attention matching, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation regimes, and data strategies ranging from real-data augmentation to synthetic and data‑free approaches. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, while important limitations remain around preserving long‑tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context‑Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied deliberately—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and inputs, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely delivers large reductions in model size and latency while preserving most task performance. Real-world success requires representation-aware objectives, options for data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, and careful evaluation under distribution shift and modality-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Duarte
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely recovers much of a teacher’s performance when practitioners choose appropriate transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational losses), align teacher and student capacity and tokenization, and combine distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, pretraining, or architecture search. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on data availability and provenance, teacher quality and friendliness, and careful selection of transfer targets; unresolved challenges include distribution shift, rare-token or long‑tail behavior, reliable data‑free distillation, and robustness or fairness under compression. Treated as a central element within hybrid compression pipelines and guided by principled signal selection and student-aware design, KD offers the best practical route to compact, high‑quality models for real-world deep learning and NLP deployments.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. When applied deliberately — selecting appropriate transfer signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods — KD routinely produces compact models with strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Real-world application requires context-aware design choices (what to transfer, how to align, and which data to use) and targeted mitigations for known failure modes such as distribution shift, rare-token degradation, bias transfer, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple logits-matching trick into a broad family of techniques for compressing or transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students. Contemporary work spans output-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, architecture-aware attention and channel-wise transfers, self- and teacher-free schemes, data-augmentation–enhanced distillation, and methods that operate without access to original training data. Empirical and analytical studies connect KD to regularization and label-smoothing phenomena, identify key tradeoffs tied to teacher quality and data availability, and show that combining KD with deployment-aware strategies (pruning, quantization, compact pretraining) yields practical, high-performing compressed models across vision and language tasks. Remaining challenges include domain shift, heterogeneous teacher–student alignment, privacy-aware distillation, and principled selection of what to transfer and when.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When designed with task- and capacity-aware choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or attention maps), and when combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies, KD routinely produces compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, its success is context-dependent: practitioner choices about teacher quality, student architecture, data provenance, selective sample usage, and evaluation under distribution shift determine whether distilled models meet production requirements.

papers_seen.author: Villarreal
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for converting large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD methods transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure and are commonly combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies. Empirical practice shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy, but realizing robust, production-ready students requires careful design choices around what is transferred, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that students retain much of the teachers' task performance while reducing inference cost and resource consumption. The practice extends beyond matching final logits to include feature- and layer-level supervision, attention- or projector-based alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data approaches). KD has been applied across modalities and deployment regimes (on-device, privacy-aware, and distributed/federated settings), and empirical work highlights both practical successes and recurring failure modes such as sensitivity to teacher-student mismatch, domain shift, and preservation of rare or low-frequency signals. Current best practices emphasize combining representation-level objectives, careful input/data handling, and co-design of teacher and student; open problems remain around robustness, heterogeneity, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Holt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving task performance. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, transferring relational structure, and leveraging multi-teacher or online schemes. KD is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with data-aware strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). Empirical evidence shows KD often yields compact models that approach teacher performance across vision, language, ranking, and detection tasks, but its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and domain-specific constraints. Key open issues include robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare-class or rare-token behavior, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors.
