papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention or relational supervision, multi- or self-teaching schedules, and data-aware or data-free protocols—and is most effective when co-designed with student architectures and complementary compression methods. Practical application requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, data access or synthesis, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is matched to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch. When designers select what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to expose the student to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online peer predictions), and how to adapt protocols for distributed or privacy-sensitive settings, KD yields large practical gains in latency, memory, and deployability while controlling risks such as bias transfer or robustness loss. A deployment-aware KD practice leverages representation-aware objectives, data-free synthesis when training data are unavailable, adversarial or online schemes for richer alignment, and federated-distillation architectures for communication-efficient collaboration.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-line, Context-aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred, how intermediate layers are aligned, and whether data or privacy constraints hold, KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in inference speed and memory. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: optimization difficulties, mismatches in capacity between teacher and student, and limited or private data require tailored objectives, architecture-aware choices, and complementary techniques. This essay argues KD should be a primary strategy in model-compression toolkits while recommending concrete practices to increase reliability across real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential and Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost, but its reliability depends on choices about what to distill, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited, heterogeneous, or private data. Realistic deployment requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, adapting the distillation signal to the task and student capacity, and evaluating robustness and privacy implications.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, privacy) while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive power. KD has grown from soft-label (logit) matching into a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer alignment, relational and contrastive signals, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. In practice KD is most effective when signals, student architecture, and data strategies are co-designed for the target task and deployment context and when KD is combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include theoretical understanding, robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors in language tasks, and distillation under data-scarce or privacy-sensitive constraints.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods include soft-output (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, and more recent data-free, multi-teacher, and online/self-distillation variants. When combined with architecture-aware transformations such as pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search, KD enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory that are critical for deploying NLP systems. Remaining challenges include distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and fine-grained behaviors, robustness under distribution shift and adversarial settings, and safeguarding fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks KD uses multiple transfer channels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and training regimes (offline teacher supervision, online co-training, multi-teacher ensembles) to recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory. Practical deployments typically combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and must manage data availability, teacher–student capacity alignment, and robustness to domain shift and rare behaviors. Remaining challenges concern data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, principled choices of which teacher signals to transfer for a given student and task, and avoiding transfer of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Sparks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone and can be adapted to diverse constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Its practical success relies on careful co‑design of teacher and student, selection of what knowledge to transfer, data strategies (including privacy‑preserving or data‑free variants), and combination with complementary compression methods. KD is best treated as a central element of compression pipelines rather than a standalone cure: when integrated with architecture-aware compression and rigorous evaluation under deployment conditions, it yields compact models that preserve much of teacher behavior while respecting resource and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Extensions, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable method for producing compact student models from larger teachers. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely yields favorable trade‑offs of accuracy, latency, and memory across speech, vision, and language tasks. However, its success depends on data availability, teacher quality, and deployment constraints; effective use treats KD as the first line of a broader, context‑aware compression pipeline rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all solution.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line, Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from soft outputs to intermediate representations and relational signals—and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment practices. While KD should be treated as a primary strategy in compression pipelines because of its empirical utility and adaptability, its reliable use requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data provenance or synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, pragmatic toolkit for compressing large or ensemble neural models into smaller, deployable students. The family of KD methods includes matching softened outputs (logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, transferring relational or contrastive signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, adversarial and ensemble-driven transfers, and data-aware or data-free variants. KD is most effective when integrated as a system-level primitive with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and when teacher–student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints are explicitly considered. Key practical concerns include teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, domain and data alignment, preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors, robustness and privacy considerations, and engineering choices about which signals to transfer and how to align layers or modules.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a pragmatic and flexible approach to compressing large neural models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in size and compute while retaining much of a teacher model's performance, and it adapts well to modalities from vision to speech and to task-specific constraints in NLP. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, mismatches between teacher and student, and the potential for poorer outcomes when distilling inappropriate teacher signals require careful method selection and evaluation. Best practice therefore combines tailored distillation architectures, curriculum or multi-teacher strategies, privacy-aware mechanisms where needed, and awareness of when label-smoothing or teacher-free alternatives are preferable.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure through a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and supports variants such as multi-teacher, online, adversarial, and data-free distillation. Its effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, what and how knowledge is transferred, data availability (or synthetic data strategies), and complementary compression mechanisms (architecture search, pruning, quantization). While KD has enabled many real-world deployments across modalities, its limits include sensitivity to distribution shift, optimization mismatches, fairness and privacy concerns, and challenges in aligning heterogeneous architectures. Best practice treats KD as a core first-line strategy combined with targeted methods tailored to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad family of techniques—matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning intermediate features or attention maps, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—enable deployment of compact models under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance in many settings, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and optimization details; careful method selection and combination with complementary compression techniques are therefore central to reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy and desirable properties. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and in how and when the transfer occurs (offline teacher-to-student, online/co-distillation, adversarial/ensemble-driven, or data-free with synthetic samples). Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical work shows strong gains in efficiency, but also highlights limitations: dependence on teacher quality and data alignment, possible degradation under domain shift or when sensitive attributes are transferred, and open problems in data-free or privacy-preserving settings. This synthesis summarizes key mechanisms, representative variants, cross-modal applications, common engineering practices, and the principal open challenges informed by recent empirical and survey literature.

papers_seen.author: Meza
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, system-level family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, compute, and privacy. Over the past decade KD has diversified from simple softened-logit matching into many practical recipes — intermediate-feature and attention matching, relation-aware losses, multi-teacher schemes, online or co-distillation, and data-free or federated variants — and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, compact pretraining) and task- or data-aware strategies. Empirical and analytic work shows KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance and sometimes improve generalization, but outcomes depend critically on what knowledge is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and optimization dynamics; open challenges remain around robustness, rare-token and long-tail behavior, privacy, and principled student design.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving predictive performance. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention-level supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, and data-centered strategies including augmentation and data-free synthesis. When combined with architecture-aware design, pretraining, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD enables practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and edge settings. However, its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, optimization dynamics, and practical concerns such as privacy, robustness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. It transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, producing models that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory. KD is broadly applicable across modalities and tasks, and its practical success increases when combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture search, pruning, representation matching) and when training pipelines are adapted to data availability, privacy constraints, and teacher–student mismatches. However, KD is not universally sufficient: distributional shifts, data heterogeneity, absence of training data, and poorly chosen teacher signals can limit effectiveness, so careful design choices and hybrid pipelines are recommended.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from one or more high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relation-aware losses, layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained transformers, self-distillation, curriculum-driven distillation, and complementary use with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and enables deployment under stringent latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervision richer than hard labels. A diverse set of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate representations and attention, relational or contrastive objectives, ensemble and online schemes, and data-aware synthesis—combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) yields compact models that often retain most of a teacher’s performance. Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data access and alignment, and optimization choices; remaining challenges include reliable data-free distillation, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, transfer of robustness and fairness properties, and reducing the computational cost of distillation itself.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals—and are often combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design). Across vision and language tasks, distillation commonly yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and evaluation under realistic deployment constraints are addressed. Important ongoing challenges include data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, robustness and fairness under compression, preserving rare-token behaviors in NLP, and principled choices about which signals to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. Over the past decade KD has diversified from soft-label (logit) matching to include intermediate-representation alignment, attention and relational supervision, contrastive and projector-based objectives, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture co-design) and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in inference cost with modest losses in task performance. Realizing these benefits in practice requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and availability, and evaluation for robustness and fairness; several open problems remain, notably reliable data-free distillation, principled teacher design, and preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their predictive power. Across vision, language, and generative settings, KD extends from simple softened-logit matching to richer objectives that mimic intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; it also supports varied training regimes including offline teacher–student, online co-training, multi-teacher curricula, and data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary methods (pretraining, architecture search, pruning, quantization, and federated procedures), KD helps meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints in real deployments. However, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, how to handle limited or absent data, and how to avoid transferring undesirable teacher behaviors—issues that remain active research directions.

papers_seen.author: Sandoval
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically oriented family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy). KD methods include matching softened outputs (logits), aligning intermediate features and attention maps, transferring relational or contrastive signals, and using multi-teacher, online, self-distillation, or data-free variants. The most reliable deployments treat KD as a system-level primitive combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful co-design of teacher, student, distillation signals, and data strategies. Key practical determinants of success are teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, the provenance and availability of distillation data (including synthetic or generated data), and explicit handling of robustness, rare-token behavior, and fairness or privacy risks. Remaining challenges center on data-free distillation, principled selection of distilled signals for heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behaviors in NLP, and automating trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad, practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, generative, and multimodal domains. Research shows KD can preserve—and in some settings improve—task performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency when combined with complementary strategies. Practical success depends on what is transferred (outputs, internal features, attention), how teacher and student are aligned architecturally and procedurally, and on data and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of objectives and training regimes—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, attention/relational signals, data- or privacy-aware synthesis, and teacher–student co-design—that together enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, available data, teacher/student compatibility, and complementary compression techniques; open challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, distillation without original data, and principled handling of heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade the technique has grown from logit-matching into a versatile toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free strategies. When combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture co-design and when teacher–student capacity and data provenance are considered, distillation routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Important practical concerns remain, including handling limited or private data, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, maintaining robustness under distribution shift, and avoiding unintended transfer of bias. This synthesis summarizes current mechanisms, common variants, practical design principles, and open problems to guide research and engineering choices for KD-based compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, multipurpose toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring information at the output level (soft targets) and across intermediate representations, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when treated as part of a broader compression strategy that aligns distillation signals to student capacity, leverages data-aware or data-free variants when needed, and combines distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, data availability and match, and careful choice of what and how to transfer; open problems include preserving rare behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and principled automation of trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy and desirable properties. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and in how and when the transfer occurs (offline teacher-to-student, online/co-distillation, adversarial/ensemble-driven, or data-free with synthetic samples). Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical work shows strong gains in efficiency, but also highlights limitations: dependence on teacher quality and data alignment, possible degradation under domain shift or when sensitive attributes are transferred, and open problems in data-free or privacy-preserving settings. This synthesis summarizes key mechanisms, representative variants, cross-modal applications, common engineering practices, and the principal open challenges informed by recent empirical and survey literature.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Principled Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' predictive power. KD is most effective when it goes beyond naïve soft-label copying: matching internal representations, aligning inputs and tokenization, choosing appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and adapting teacher updates or curricula all materially affect transfer quality. KD should be used as part of a broader compression pipeline (architecture design, quantization, pruning, or data strategies) and with explicit checks for rare-token behavior, fairness, and robustness. When applied with these considerations, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for production constraints in vision, language, and other modalities.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Motivations, and Open Questions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques that transfer information from larger or more complex models (teachers) to smaller or more efficient models (students). These practices are used both to reduce inference cost and to adapt large models to constrained or specialized settings (privacy-preserving deployment, edge devices, or faster generation). Across applications—classification, sequence modeling, graph learning, speech, and machine translation—research has explored what to transfer (logits, features, representations), how to transfer it (soft labels, feature projectors, adversarial objectives, data augmentation), and when transfer can fail or require modification (noisy labels, distributional shifts, imperfect teachers). Empirical and theoretical work shows benefits but also identifies trade-offs (regularization vs. fidelity, robustness transfer limits, and data requirements), motivating hybrid approaches that combine pre-training, careful sample selection, and augmentation.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings, KD variants—ranging from logits or soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, many-to-many layer mapping, meta-learned teachers, data-free synthesis, and federated or device-aware schemes—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher utility. Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, choosing appropriate distillation targets and curricula, and combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Remaining gaps include optimization dynamics, data- and privacy-limited scenarios, theoretical explanations of when distillation helps, and robustness to distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — including softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with architectural or numerical compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data availability, and optimization dynamics are considered; however, its success is contingent on capacity alignment, data choices, and safeguards against transferring undesirable behaviors. Applications range from accelerated inference and edge deployment to domain adaptation, federated learning, and task-specific adaptations such as non-autoregressive translation and graph-to-MLP compression.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students that preserve much of task performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi‑teacher), and data strategies (real, augmented, synthetic, and data‑free), and it integrates naturally with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture co‑design. Treated as a default first‑line strategy, KD should be applied with explicit attention to teacher–student co‑design, data provenance, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare‑token behaviors; where those safeguards are impractical, alternative or complementary compression steps are required. This paper argues that KD be adopted as the standard initial approach for model compression in deep learning and NLP, while documenting its typical failure modes and practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has branched from simple soft-target matching into a family of methods including logits and feature matching, layer-wise and task-aware distillation, self- and online-distillation, data-free or adversarial sample synthesis, and strategies for low-precision or few-shot deployment. Practical success depends on matching the distilled signal to student capacity, handling limited or private data, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (e.g., pruning and quantization). Open challenges remain around robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, preventing harmful bias transfer, and building stronger theoretical predictions of when and how distillation succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a family of methods that include feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and projection, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and careful design choices about which signals to transfer. Open challenges include handling distribution shift, preserving rare-class or rare-token behavior, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or undesirable behaviors. This synthesis summarizes common methods, mechanisms, practical patterns, and outstanding limitations to guide researchers and practitioners applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Dependent Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD operates through multiple mechanisms — softened-output transfer, intermediate-representation matching, relational and contrastive objectives, and synthetic-data strategies — and is most effective when treated as a system-level design choice that aligns teacher signals, student capacity, and available data. While KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, its reliability depends on careful co-design, complementary compression methods, and explicit handling of domain shift, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary strategies—pre-training compact architectures, feature-level supervision, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis or augmentation, and task-aware student design—KD yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, and data availability; without such care, distillation can underperform or lose task-specific signals. I argue KD should be the first-line approach for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, provided practitioners adopt principled, context-aware distillation recipes.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Rationale, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, flexible pathway to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Treated as a system-level toolkit rather than a single loss term, KD supports multiple transfer channels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Successful deployment requires careful teacher–student alignment, data or synthetic-data strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-token or fine-grained behavior. I argue KD should be the default first‑line strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP while being applied deliberately and combined with complementary compression primitives and validation under realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, System‑Level Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. Treated as a system-level strategy—one that selects what knowledge to transfer, aligns teacher and student capacity, and composes with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies)—KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for many practical applications. However, its success is conditional: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns constrain outcomes, so KD must be applied thoughtfully and evaluated across deployment metrics.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD spans logit-level supervision, representation- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, and specialized adaptations for data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful teacher–student co‑design, KD routinely produces compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. Nonetheless, success depends on signal choice, capacity alignment, data provenance, and attention to robustness, fairness, and distribution shift; several open technical and evaluation questions remain for production deployment.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression techniques transfer behaviors of large models into smaller, more efficient models by supervising students with information derived from teachers (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention, or synthetic labels). Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing size and latency. Effective practice combines choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data strategies (including augmentation or synthesis), and complementary structural compression. Remaining challenges include handling imperfect teachers, limited or private data, robustness and out-of-distribution behavior, and principled automation of trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple softened-target matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online regimes, adversarial decision-boundary techniques, and data-aware or data-free strategies. When integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility and data provenance, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Important limitations remain, including sensitivity to distribution shift, data- and privacy-constrained settings, preserving long-tail behaviors, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher biases; addressing these issues requires pipeline-oriented, context-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible supervision (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensemble signals) and interoperates with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data synthesis). When used systematically—selecting what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, leveraging data-aware or data-free strategies, and integrating KD into broader compression pipelines—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployments. At the same time, careful attention to teacher quality, rare-token preservation, robustness, and domain shift is required to avoid predictable failure modes and to maximize real-world utility.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision and natural language tasks, distinct distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relations) and procedures (layer-wise mapping, task-aware filtering, ensemble distillation, and integration with low-precision or pruning techniques) enable large reductions in compute and memory with modest performance loss. Practical success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and targeted design choices that select what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression (with System‑Level Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported method for converting large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students. When co‑designed with student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD delivers large real‑world gains in latency, memory, and deployability; however, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multi‑Strategy, Practical — but Bounded — Path for Compressing Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. When applied thoughtfully — combining soft-label transfer with representation-level guidance, architecture-aware design, and data strategies — KD enables compact models that meet memory, latency, and deployment constraints while retaining most of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: limited or private data, teacher errors, student capacity gaps, and robustness or fairness concerns create concrete failure modes that require complementary methods and careful evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a multi-strategy engineering approach whose best results arise from combining several targeted techniques that suit task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Model Compression: A Practical, Context‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, system-level strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students. KD provides flexible transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data synthesis). However, its reliable use requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data provenance and coverage, robustness and adversarial properties, and mechanisms for heterogeneous architectures. When adopted as a design paradigm rather than a single loss term, KD delivers the best trade-offs for accuracy, latency, and resource constraints across vision and NLP tasks.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods include transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and data-free or few-shot variants to handle limited or private data. Best results come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that also incorporates architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. KD is therefore a central tool for efficient deployment, but it has clear limits and must be designed carefully to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or losing rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models: Evidence, Techniques, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool to compress large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, KD has enabled domain adaptation, model-size reduction, cross-lingual transfer, and deployment under resource constraints. Success depends on (1) aligning teacher and student inputs and intermediate representations, (2) choosing appropriate supervision signals (soft labels, intermediate-feature losses, attention-based guidance), (3) handling the absence of original training data when necessary, and (4) adapting compression to task and domain requirements. This review synthesizes empirical and methodological findings from recent studies to recommend principled KD choices for practitioners aiming to deploy compact, robust models in real-world NLP and related tasks.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression: Effectiveness, Limits, and Practical Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When treated as a system—choosing which signals to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning teacher and student architectures, managing data and sample selection, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks. Its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and attention to robustness and rare-token behavior; hence KD is best used as the central element of a broader compression pipeline rather than as a standalone fix.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a practical toolkit, KD offers multiple forms of supervision (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational signals) and composes naturally with structural compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When applied as part of a system-level pipeline that co-designs student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression steps, KD reliably produces compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and careful selection of what and how to transfer. Responsible deployment therefore requires explicit practices to mitigate degraded rare-token behavior, distribution shift, privacy leakage, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature has converged on a set of recurring methods (soft-target/logit supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware protocols) and deployment practices (combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Empirical evidence demonstrates that appropriately designed distillation pipelines often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and distributional alignment. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors (especially in NLP), and principled teacher–student co-design and curricula for difficult tasks.
