papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher(s) to student(s). Advances span logit- and feature-based matching, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, data-free and federated scenarios, and domain- or task-specific adaptations in NLP. Practical work shows KD can yield large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but design choices (what to match, how to weight teachers, whether data are available, and deployment constraints) strongly affect outcomes. Remaining challenges include robustness to domain shift, privacy and communication constraints in distributed settings, and principled handling of teacher–student mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Principled Use of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, practical method for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. However, its success is conditional: choices about what to transfer, how to supervise internal representations, how to design student architectures for particular tasks, and how to handle data, distribution shift, and fairness constraints materially affect outcomes. I argue that KD should be treated as a flexible design pattern—combining soft-target transfer, internal-representation matching, task-adaptive architecture design, and explicit fairness or data strategies—to produce reliable, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. Treated as a toolbox of complementary signals and regimes—soft logits, intermediate representation matching, attention and relational objectives, multi‑teacher schedules, and data-aware variants—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when co-designed with student architectures and deployment constraints. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit evaluation of robustness, long‑tail behaviors, and fairness, so KD should be applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a universal remedy.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses or transfers knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) by using richer supervision than hard labels alone. The literature has developed multiple complementary strategies—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, architecturally guided replacement, multi-teacher schedules, data- and privacy-aware variants, and teacher-training schemes—to address deployment constraints, domain shift, and limited or private data. Empirical work shows these approaches can close much of the performance gap to full-size models across classification, language understanding, and retrieval tasks; theoretical and empirical analyses explain why distillation often improves generalization beyond mere compression. Remaining challenges include input distribution mismatch, low-frequency token fidelity in sequence tasks, and robust distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Schwartz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical approach for converting large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer richer supervision than hard labels alone (logit/soft-targets, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals), and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical results across language and vision tasks show KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance while substantially lowering inference cost, but effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability or synthesis strategies, and careful selection of distillation targets and training schedules. Remaining challenges include preserving rare-token or long‑tail behaviors, maintaining robustness and fairness under compression, and automating student design for constrained budgets.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad, practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, generative, and multimodal domains. Research shows KD can preserve—and in some settings improve—task performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency when combined with complementary strategies. Practical success depends on what is transferred (outputs, internal features, attention), how teacher and student are aligned architecturally and procedurally, and on data and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring the predictive behavior and internal representations of large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD encompasses soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational objectives, and a range of training regimes (offline teacher supervision, online co-distillation, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or black-box variants). Treated as a system-level tool and combined with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. Important practical constraints include teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or privacy constraints, and the need to preserve robustness, rare-token behavior, and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Path to Compact NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When combined with complementary strategies—appropriate pretraining, architecture-aware compression, data management, or teacher-free alternatives—KD can produce compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. However, KD is not a universal remedy: success depends on what is distilled, how student and teacher are matched, the availability and provenance of data, and the need to manage transferred biases, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Primary, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation signals (logits, features, attention), accounting for teacher–student capacity, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces memory, compute, and latency burdens while enabling deployment across edge, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, KD is not a universal cure: its benefits depend on optimization, data availability, and robustness/fairness goals, and practical deployments require matching KD variants to constraints and verifying student behavior under distribution shift and adversarial threats.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervision richer than hard labels. A diverse set of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate representations and attention, relational or contrastive objectives, ensemble and online schemes, and data-aware synthesis—combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) yields compact models that often retain most of a teacher’s performance. Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data access and alignment, and optimization choices; remaining challenges include reliable data-free distillation, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, transfer of robustness and fairness properties, and reducing the computational cost of distillation itself.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameters and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance. When combined with complementary compression tools and careful teacher–student co-design, distillation provides a practical first-line strategy for real-world model compression, though important open problems remain around fairness, data availability, heterogeneity, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher→student soft-label transfer into a broad toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across vision, language, and multimodal domains. Contemporary approaches extend logits matching to representation- and structure-aware objectives, multi- and continual-teaching schemes, task-aware layer selection, and combinations with pruning or architecture-level compression. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints but its success depends on design choices about what is transferred, how the student is supervised, data availability, and student capacity. Practical progress emphasizes representation matching beyond logits, careful layer- and channel-level alignment, and composing KD with other compression techniques; remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, data-free scenarios, and preserving fine-grained or safety-critical behavior.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of methods for converting large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. Across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks, practitioners apply a spectrum of KD objectives — from softened-logit supervision to representation and relation matching, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and data-free approaches — and combine KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when teacher–student capacity, data availability, and the form of transferred signal are well matched. Open challenges include theoretical characterization of transfer, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors in language models, robust distillation under domain shift, and privacy-aware or data-free compression regimes.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. A spectrum of KD strategies has been developed—soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, self-distillation, and data-free variants—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows well-designed distillation pipelines can recover much of a teacher’s performance while delivering large gains in latency and memory, but outcomes depend on the choice of distillation signal, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints such as domain shift and privacy. Current practical directions emphasize representation-aware objectives, layer-alignment techniques, and hybrid pipelines that treat KD as a core element of system-level compression.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, privacy) while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive power. KD has grown from soft-label (logit) matching into a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer alignment, relational and contrastive signals, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. In practice KD is most effective when signals, student architecture, and data strategies are co-designed for the target task and deployment context and when KD is combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include theoretical understanding, robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors in language tasks, and distillation under data-scarce or privacy-sensitive constraints.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teachers. Techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), how teachers are chosen or ensembled, and whether distillation is done with or without access to original data. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data augmentation, or synthetic-data generation) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, success depends on careful objective design, alignment of teacher and student capacity, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as degraded handling of low‑frequency tokens, adversarial vulnerability, or erased relative class information.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a unified, pragmatic pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, augmenting or synthesizing data when necessary, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD consistently yields large efficiency gains (memory, compute, latency) while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and multimodal settings. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and robustness concerns, and practical pipelines must address these limits through curriculum design, data-aware augmentation, and careful choice of distillation targets.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Powerful, Multifaceted, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and versatile approach for compressing deep models for deployment in constrained environments. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal information from larger teachers to smaller students using a range of targets and training regimes; when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression steps, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. However, the method’s effectiveness depends on careful selection of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable teacher behavior, so KD should be applied as part of an integrated compression strategy rather than a single silver-bullet solution.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. The field comprises a family of methods that transfer different forms of information—from soft logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational structure—and integrates naturally with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Success depends on choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, managing data availability (including data-free or federated setups), and designing appropriate optimization curricula. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, rare-token preservation in NLP, and robustness under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable design paradigm—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely achieves strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher quality, and evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints; practitioners should therefore apply KD together with targeted validation, robustness checks, and complementary engineering such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated pathway to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD encompasses multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and operates across modes (offline, online, ensemble, data-free). When co‑designed with student architectures and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs for vision and language models. However, practical success requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, and robustness to domain shift and rare behaviors. The method is best treated as a default, context‑aware tool that should be adapted—rather than assumed universal—for each deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both deep learning and NLP. KD provides flexible supervision (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensemble signals) and interoperates with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data synthesis). When used systematically—selecting what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, leveraging data-aware or data-free strategies, and integrating KD into broader compression pipelines—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployments. At the same time, careful attention to teacher quality, rare-token preservation, robustness, and domain shift is required to avoid predictable failure modes and to maximize real-world utility.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for converting large teacher models into compact, deployable students. When applied as a context-aware, system-level strategy and combined with complementary methods (architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for NLP and broader deep-learning tasks. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and careful evaluation of robustness, rare-token behaviors, and privacy. Treating KD as the first-line tool within an integrated compression pipeline—rather than a one-size-fits-all loss—delivers the most reliable outcomes while pointing to open research on robustness, data-free distillation, and privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a core tool for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Evidence across vision, multimodal, and NLP tasks shows distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling quantization, faster inference, and privacy-aware deployment. However, distillation is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, data unavailability, modality mismatches, and safety/robustness concerns can limit how closely a student can match its teacher. Combining complementary techniques—feature-level mimicry, intermediate-attention alignment, multi-teacher schedules, confidence-weighted losses, and generative or data-free strategies—yields the most reliable compressed models in practice.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. When applied as part of a system-level compression pipeline that co-designs student architectures, distillation objectives, and data strategies, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. Effective use of KD requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, available data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or federated protocols). Despite strong empirical results across modalities, open challenges persist in robustness, rare-token behavior, privacy, and theoretical understanding, motivating careful evaluation and targeted remedies in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking large models: it is a versatile family of techniques that can preserve performance while enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but it must be adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. Effective KD requires attention to the teacher-student relationship (including training teachers that are "student-friendly"), to data availability (including data-free approaches), and to distributional mismatches (e.g., federated or heterogeneous-device scenarios). When such concerns are addressed—via task-adaptive compression, feature- or relation-aware transfer, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, or methods that expose raw data signals lost in naive distillation—KD can deliver near-teacher performance at far lower cost. However, KD has known failure modes (such as propagating teacher errors on low-frequency tokens or degrading under data heterogeneity) that demand targeted remedies. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an adaptable design pattern: choose techniques that match your downstream objective (accuracy, latency, privacy, heterogeneity) rather than applying a one-size-fits-all distillation loss.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. A broad set of practical recipes—including logit (soft-target) supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, many-to-many layer alignment, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and joint use with architecture search, pruning, or quantization—enable deployment of compact models across vision, language, and graph tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while reducing compute and memory, but effectiveness depends on the choice of transfer target, availability or synthesis of suitable data, student architecture, and training dynamics. Key open issues remain around principled explanations for when distillation helps, reliably transferring robustness and fairness properties, privacy-aware distillation, and automating student design for specific resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and device constraints. Over the past decade KD has expanded from softened-logit transfer to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online regimes, and data-aware strategies (including data-free synthesis). KD is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and when practitioners address teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and evaluation of robustness and fairness. Important practical limits remain: capacity mismatch, degraded transfer for rare or domain-specific behaviors, and distribution shift, which all motivate careful selection of distilled signals, student co-design, and validation under realistic deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible method to produce compact models from larger teachers by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. As a system-level primitive KD interoperates with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies to yield strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs in real deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, data provenance or synthesis, and explicit validation for robustness, fairness, and rare-token behaviors. Treated as a first‑line tool with targeted validation and complementary methods, KD offers the best pragmatic path to deployable compact models in many deep-learning and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven strategy for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller students suitable for real-world deployment. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher model’s utility. However, KD is not a single recipe: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), how teachers and students are aligned, and the availability and provenance of data. Treating KD as a system-level primitive — combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), informed data strategies, and careful evaluation of robustness and fairness — yields the best practical tradeoffs while highlighting open challenges in few-shot, privacy-sensitive, and domain-shifted settings.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, practitioners use softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, attention- or relation-level signals, multi-teacher and online schedules, and self-distillation. Distillation is typically combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with data strategies that range from using distilled teacher outputs to synthetic or data-free approaches. Empirical successes include large reductions in inference cost while preserving most of the teacher’s performance, but failures arise when teacher–student misalignment, data mismatch, low-frequency outputs, or privacy constraints are not addressed. Practical pipelines treat distillation as a flexible, context-aware toolkit rather than a fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD operates at multiple levels — softened output distributions, intermediate feature or attention imitation, and relational or layer-wise alignment — and composes naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD yields substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy for deployed systems, but its success depends on careful design choices related to what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Practical deployment treats KD as a core element of a hybrid compression pipeline, with task-aware signal selection, student-aware teacher design, and targeted remedies for distribution shift, low-frequency phenomena, adversarial vulnerability, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD spans soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, layer-aware alignment, self-distillation, and architecture-replacement strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture changes), KD enables practical tradeoffs between accuracy, latency, and memory for NLP and other modalities. Effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, what form of knowledge is transferred, and constraints such as data availability, privacy, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically effective approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment. When combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, careful attention to data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and domain shift is required to preserve robustness and rare or domain-specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Burns
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the System-Level Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best framed not as a single loss but as the central, system-level mechanism around which practical model-compression pipelines should be organized. When combined with representation-aware objectives, teacher–student design, data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving approaches), and complementary structural compression, KD produces compact, deployable models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. Practical success requires careful alignment of what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, relational or attention signals), awareness of teacher–student capacity and domain mismatch, and explicit strategies for settings with no or private data. I argue that treating KD as the organizing principle for compression accelerates deployment while focusing research on the remaining gaps: robustness under domain shift, preserving rare-token behaviors, and principled data-free or privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression: A Pipeline‑Oriented, Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core and first‑line strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students, but only when embedded in a carefully designed pipeline. KD’s value comes from its flexibility — it can transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and be applied offline, online, or with synthetic/data‑free inputs — and from its ability to compose with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies. Yet KD is not a universal remedy: outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality and suitability, student capacity and architecture, availability and domain match of data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy. The recommended stance is pragmatic: prioritize KD as the core compression tool, combine it with complementary structural and data techniques, adopt teacher‑aware and student‑aware design (including meta‑teaching and targeted sample strategies), and evaluate compressed models under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses soft‑label (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and online schemes, self‑distillation, and data‑free synthesis. Across vision, speech, and natural language applications, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when carefully designed; its empirical success depends on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, data availability or synthesis, and complementary compression steps such as pruning or quantization. Important open issues include robustness under domain shift, preservation of rare or safety‑critical behavior, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or undesirable properties.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Armstrong
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability or synthesis, and training schedules; open problems include reliable data-free distillation, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and principled theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a broadly useful, pragmatic approach for shrinking large models into deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. Treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. When combined with complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization) and student-aware curricula, KD frequently achieves large reductions in memory and latency while retaining most of teacher performance. However, realizing these gains in production requires careful attention to what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Integrated Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, flexible means to produce compact models for deployment in compute-, memory-, or privacy-constrained settings. When chosen and applied with attention to what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression techniques, KD reliably yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits depend on principled design and evaluation, and it should be integrated into broader compression pipelines rather than used in isolation.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels—such as softened logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational constraints—and is typically integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware choices (data augmentation, synthetic data, or privacy‑aware aggregation) to meet latency, memory, and device constraints. Its success depends on deliberate design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and availability, and training schedules; common failure modes include degraded rare-token behavior, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, and privacy or robustness concerns. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable core of compression, combined with monitoring and targeted mitigations for known limits.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression: Powerful, Practical, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and optimization interactions. I argue that KD should serve as the default first-line method in compression toolkits, but practitioners must treat it as a design paradigm that is complemented by targeted validation and additional compression methods where needed.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD has evolved from soft‑target (logit) matching into a broad toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention matching, multi‑teacher and online schemes, task‑aware student design, and data‑aware strategies (including data‑free and privacy‑sensitive workflows). Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision and NLP when distillation is combined with appropriate student architectures, careful selection of transfer targets, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, reliable transfer of rare or long‑tail behaviors, and robust distillation when training data are limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring supervisory signals that go beyond hard labels. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, KD methods—ranging from softened-logit matching to intermediate representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher schedules, self-distillation, and data‑free variants—regularly improve the accuracy–efficiency trade-off. Practical deployments co-design distillation targets, student architectures, and data strategies, and they often combine KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Important limitations remain, including sensitivity to teacher–student capacity mismatch, reduced fidelity on rare or low-frequency behaviors in NLP, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable distillation without access to original training data. Addressing these challenges requires hybrid pipelines, better teacher selection, and principled data- or privacy-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, pragmatic toolkit for compressing large or ensemble neural models into smaller, deployable students. The family of KD methods includes matching softened outputs (logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, transferring relational or contrastive signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, adversarial and ensemble-driven transfers, and data-aware or data-free variants. KD is most effective when integrated as a system-level primitive with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and when teacher–student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints are explicitly considered. Key practical concerns include teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, domain and data alignment, preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors, robustness and privacy considerations, and engineering choices about which signals to transfer and how to align layers or modules.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied deliberately — choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and handling data- and deployment-specific constraints — KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, distillation is not automatic: outcomes depend on teacher strength and training, student architecture and capacity, the form of distilled signals, data availability (including data‑free settings), and fairness/privacy goals. Best practice treats KD as a core component combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and deployment-aware procedures to produce reliable, efficient models for real applications.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, and generation tasks. Contemporary KD methods extend far beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, curriculum and online schemes, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and tight integrations with architecture-level compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends on matched teacher–student design, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthetic-data alternatives, and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-class behaviors. Open challenges remain in domain-shift robustness, privacy-sensitive distillation, automated student architecture design, and principled selection of which aspects of teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a practical, multi‑purpose toolkit that enables substantial efficiency gains when compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods—ranging from soft‑target matching to feature and attention imitation, multi‑teacher schedules, and data‑synthesis—regularly yield favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, but their real‑world success requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle limited or private data and distribution shifts.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s capability. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, transferring intermediate representations or attentions, leveraging ensembles or self-teaching, and operating in constrained settings via data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Across vision, generative models, and natural language tasks, distillation is used both as a standalone compression technique and as a complement to pruning and quantization. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability, and how to mitigate optimization and distributional mismatches. While KD often produces compact models that approach teacher performance, practical deployment requires careful design to avoid failure modes arising from heterogeneous data, limited student capacity, or misaligned training objectives.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Conditional, Pipeline‑Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD routinely yields students that approach teacher performance across tasks when practitioners attend to what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data are handled. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design. I argue that KD should be treated as the practical core or first‑line strategy for model compression, but only when it is applied as part of a careful pipeline that combines complementary compression techniques, explicit robustness and fairness checks, and data-aware distillation practices.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and compression seek to retain performance of large deep models while reducing size and latency for deployment. Methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include transferring internal representations, attention maps, and relational or adversarial signals; they can be applied during pretraining, task fine-tuning, or domain adaptation, and may operate with or without access to original training data. Empirical results across retrieval, reading comprehension, pretrained language models, and other domains show consistent trade-offs where careful choice of distillation targets, training curricula, and data augmentation materially improves student generalization and robustness while substantially lowering compute and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Crawford
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple teacher‑student recipe into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and explicitly addressing robustness and distributional shifts. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, training regimes, practical recommendations, and remaining challenges for KD-driven model compression in deep learning and NLP.
