papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multi‑Strategy Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is most useful when treated as a system-level, context-sensitive toolkit rather than a single loss term. Properly designed distillation pipelines combine multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals), teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, data provenance (including options for data-free distillation), and explicit evaluation of robustness, rare-token fidelity, and fairness. A pragmatic research and engineering agenda focuses on matching distillation signals to student capacity, designing student-friendly teachers, integrating online and multi-teacher regimes where appropriate, and developing reliable data-free or privacy-aware procedures.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and adversarially or synthetically generated inputs. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data strategies, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success depends on careful matching of what is transferred to student capacity, handling data scarcity or distribution shift, and mitigating propagation of teacher errors. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, representative algorithmic families, empirical patterns, and actionable recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, insights, and practical trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in latency-, memory-, and compute-constrained settings. Work across speech, NLP, vision, and graph domains demonstrates a spectrum of approaches: matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressively replacing modules, augmenting or synthesizing training data for better student generalization, and compressing ensembles into single models. Empirical results show substantial speed and size gains with modest accuracy loss when methods are carefully matched to task and architecture. Important themes include (1) the role of dark/soft labels vs. intermediate feature signals, (2) architectural or task-aware compression (including search), (3) techniques that increase the student’s exposure to informative training points (e.g., mixup or adversarial examples), and (4) distillation strategies tailored for ensembles or heterogeneous teacher–student pairs. Open challenges remain in principled sample selection, robust transfer of inductive biases, and automated trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practices and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from a high-capacity source (teacher) to a smaller target (student). Across vision, speech, and NLP, practitioners combine logit-based supervision, feature imitation, data augmentation, and architectural or precision changes to preserve performance while shrinking computation. Recent work emphasizes (1) the role of pre-training for compact models, (2) task- and modality-specific distillation recipes, (3) data-availability and privacy constraints that motivate data-free or augmentation-based approaches, and (4) designing teachers or training procedures that improve transfer. These trends point toward hybrid pipelines that integrate pre-training, augmentation, and teacher-student co-design to get robust, efficient models for real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable design paradigm—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely achieves strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher quality, and evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints; practitioners should therefore apply KD together with targeted validation, robustness checks, and complementary engineering such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade a diverse family of distillation methods has emerged—logit-level soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, data-free or zero-shot synthesis, multi-teacher ensembles, and privacy-aware adaptations—applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative models. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data availability and domain mismatch; combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture search, quantization) and task-aware pipelines yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for turning large, high-performance neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Over the past decade KD has broadened from matching softened teacher outputs to a family of techniques that include intermediate representation matching, attention- and relation-based losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free synthesis. Successful compression with KD depends not only on the choice of distillation signal but also on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis strategies, and complementary compression primitives. Important practical concerns remain: preserving rare or domain-specific behavior in NLP, robustness and fairness under compression, and principled design choices under limited or private data. This paper synthesizes what is known about KD’s mechanisms, variants, empirical strengths, and practical limitations, and it outlines pragmatic recommendations for deploying KD in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated pathway to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD encompasses multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and operates across modes (offline, online, ensemble, data-free). When co‑designed with student architectures and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs for vision and language models. However, practical success requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, and robustness to domain shift and rare behaviors. The method is best treated as a default, context‑aware tool that should be adapted—rather than assumed universal—for each deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compressing and Deploying Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible technique that enables transferring predictive power from large models into smaller or more efficient ones. When combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, task-aware selection of distilled signals, quantization-aware training, and privacy-preserving or federated protocols, KD can make state-of-the-art models practically usable on resource-constrained and heterogeneous devices. However, realizing these gains requires attention to what is distilled (outputs versus internal representations), how distilled signals are selected for the target task, and whether data-privacy or communication constraints demand synthetic or distributed distillation procedures.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under resource constraints. Rather than a single algorithm, KD comprises multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) that should be chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and downstream requirements. Effective compression usually combines KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization) and careful alignment between teacher and student. Practical success thus depends on design choices and trade-offs rather than a universal distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically grounded approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely produces favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when practitioners choose what signals to transfer (logits, intermediate features, relational signals), align teacher and student architectures, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on data availability, teacher quality and design, teacher–student compatibility, and evaluation under distribution shift and fairness constraints. Responsible deployment therefore requires principled choices about distilled signals, data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Mechanisms, and Necessary Safeguards
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable toolkit for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When co-designed with student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD frequently yields large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: careful choice of distilled signals, training curricula, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy is required to avoid failure modes and to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from teacher models. A rich toolbox has emerged—ranging from softened-output matching to intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with structural compression—that makes it possible to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints across vision and language tasks. Practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, choice of distilled signals, data availability, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and domain-specific behavior, and principled handling of teacher–student mismatch in heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade the technique has grown from logit-matching into a versatile toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free strategies. When combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture co-design and when teacher–student capacity and data provenance are considered, distillation routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Important practical concerns remain, including handling limited or private data, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, maintaining robustness under distribution shift, and avoiding unintended transfer of bias. This synthesis summarizes current mechanisms, common variants, practical design principles, and open problems to guide research and engineering choices for KD-based compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameters and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance. When combined with complementary compression tools and careful teacher–student co-design, distillation provides a practical first-line strategy for real-world model compression, though important open problems remain around fairness, data availability, heterogeneity, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework that enables transferring predictive power from large, expensive models to smaller, deployable ones. KD supports diverse practical constraints — absent training data, limited downstream-task data, domain shifts, multi-task settings, and architectural mismatches — and couples naturally with automated model search and targeted feature imitation. By viewing KD as a family of techniques (logit transfer, feature mimicking, adversarial-sample guidance, synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-ensemble strategies) practitioners can compress models while retaining or even improving task-relevant inductive structure and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature has converged on a set of recurring methods (soft-target/logit supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware protocols) and deployment practices (combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Empirical evidence demonstrates that appropriately designed distillation pipelines often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and distributional alignment. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors (especially in NLP), and principled teacher–student co-design and curricula for difficult tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A diverse set of KD mechanisms — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance, self-distillation, and curriculum or task-aware schedules — has been developed and validated across vision, language, and domain-specific tasks. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, leveraging data or synthetic-data strategies when needed, and combining KD with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Important open challenges include transferring rare-token or long-tail behavior, preserving robustness and fairness under distribution shift, and automating student design for target resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that meet deployment constraints in compute, memory, latency, and privacy. When integrated with complementary techniques (layer mapping, data strategies, adversarial training, and architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss across vision and language tasks. Realizing these gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be a first-line strategy in compression pipelines while outlining practical caveats and design recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how training is scheduled (offline, online, self-distillation, adversarial compression). Empirical work shows KD can enable deployable models across vision, speech, and NLP, but success depends on aligning teacher-student inputs and representations, addressing optimization mismatches, and adapting objectives to task and data constraints. Open challenges include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness, fairness, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Newton
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile, widely applied approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teacher networks. KD encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms (softened outputs, intermediate representation matching, attention and relational objectives), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data‑constrained variants), and is commonly combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, and architecture design) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical results across vision, detection, speech/lipreading, and machine translation show substantial accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs when KD is carefully designed; however, reliable production usage requires deliberate teacher–student co‑design, data strategies for scarce or private data, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as teacher bias, long‑tail/rare‑token degradation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Practical Core, Proven Techniques, and Contextual Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, speech, and NLP demonstrates that students trained with distilled signals can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory. Practical success depends on choices about what form of knowledge is transferred (logits, features, attention, relations), how teacher and student capacities are aligned, and how data (real, synthetic, or none) are used. Best practices combine targeted distillation objectives, careful architecture- and capacity-aware design, and complementary compression methods; open problems remain in low-resource or data-free settings, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving rare-token or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied deliberately — choosing what form of knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle data and deployment constraints — KD routinely yields favorable tradeoffs between model compactness and retained performance. However, distillation is not automatic: data availability, teacher–student mismatches, and application-specific constraints (latency, privacy, heterogeneity) shape both achievable gains and failure modes. Best practice therefore combines representation-aware objectives, curriculum or annealing schedules, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance where helpful, and deployment-aware mechanisms such as data-free generation or privacy-preserving aggregation to realize robust, efficient students.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — including softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with architectural or numerical compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data availability, and optimization dynamics are considered; however, its success is contingent on capacity alignment, data choices, and safeguards against transferring undesirable behaviors. Applications range from accelerated inference and edge deployment to domain adaptation, federated learning, and task-specific adaptations such as non-autoregressive translation and graph-to-MLP compression.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s capability. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, transferring intermediate representations or attentions, leveraging ensembles or self-teaching, and operating in constrained settings via data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Across vision, generative models, and natural language tasks, distillation is used both as a standalone compression technique and as a complement to pruning and quantization. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability, and how to mitigate optimization and distributional mismatches. While KD often produces compact models that approach teacher performance, practical deployment requires careful design to avoid failure modes arising from heterogeneous data, limited student capacity, or misaligned training objectives.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features/attention, relational or structural signals) and can be applied in offline, online, ensemble, or data-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can deliver large efficiency gains with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy, but success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical deployments typically combine KD with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require design attention to robustness, domain shift, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for converting large pretrained models into smaller, deployable students. As a system-level design primitive it enables multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and can be adapted through data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or privacy-aware protocols). While KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, its reliable deployment requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle limited or sensitive data, distribution shift, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and distributed settings KD often recovers much of a teacher's predictive performance while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and deployment under resource or privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: outcomes depend on what signals are transferred (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, availability and quality of data (including data-free or federated setups), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats distillation as one element of a compression pipeline that combines representation matching, architecture-aware student design, data strategies, and risk-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates a broad set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal signals from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, ensemble-to-single transfer, online and self-distillation, and data-free methods that synthesize or generate surrogate inputs. Successful application typically co-designs student architectures, selects appropriate distillation signals, and adapts training and data strategies; remaining gaps include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, handling heterogeneous deployment (including federated settings), and principled guidance for choosing distillation targets across tasks.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks KD variants—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention patterns, multi-teacher and progressive schemes, and self-distillation—have enabled compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success typically requires co-design of the distillation signal, student architecture, data and augmentation choices, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., quantization or pruning). Persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, handling limited or private data, preserving rare-token and robustness properties, and automating trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it is a flexible, multi-signal toolkit that preserves much of a teacher’s performance while enabling large gains in latency, memory, and deployability. KD combines naturally with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). Its reliable use requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate and mitigate risks such as degraded long-tail behavior, robustness failures, and privacy leakage.
