papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger, higher-capacity teacher models into compact student models. KD methods span output-level soft-target matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance, and data-aware or data-free training regimes. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation strategy is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. While distilled students frequently recover most of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, core challenges remain around distilling across heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, ensuring robustness and fairness, and operating when original training data are private or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression: Effectiveness, Mechanisms, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable strategy to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD succeeds best when treated as a system-level primitive—co-designed with student architectures, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search)—and when practitioners use representation-aware objectives, careful layer alignment, and data-aware curricula. KD has clear empirical benefits across vision and NLP but also predictable limits: mismatched teacher–student capacity, scarce or altered data, and long‑tail or rare-token behaviors can reduce transfer quality. Practical deployments therefore require targeted interventions (e.g., projector layers, multi-signal transfer, synthesized data, and robustness checks) to realize reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Core, Methods, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for converting large pretrained models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. When applied with attention to what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how teacher and student are aligned (architecture-aware objectives, projectors, layer selection), and how data constraints are handled (data augmentation, data-free synthesis, privacy-aware workflows), KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across NLP and multimodal tasks. Nevertheless, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, and robustness under distribution shift, so practitioners should pair KD with complementary compression tools and task-aware evaluations to deploy compact models reliably.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Synthesizing Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students so that deployed systems meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a family of mechanisms — soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, relation- or attention-based transfer, and data-side interventions — that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical results show that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and augmentation, architecture compatibility, and robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, practitioners use softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, attention- or relation-level signals, multi-teacher and online schedules, and self-distillation. Distillation is typically combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with data strategies that range from using distilled teacher outputs to synthetic or data-free approaches. Empirical successes include large reductions in inference cost while preserving most of the teacher’s performance, but failures arise when teacher–student misalignment, data mismatch, low-frequency outputs, or privacy constraints are not addressed. Practical pipelines treat distillation as a flexible, context-aware toolkit rather than a fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical toolkit for turning large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Methods vary from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, latency, and energy, but success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, optimization choices, and targeted handling of robustness, low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive settings. Important open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, preserving rare-token and domain-specific signals, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers or data are scarce, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically supported path to compress large models into compact, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a central design pattern rather than a single loss term, KD enables multiple transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and online schedules, and integration with architecture-aware design and other compression methods. Practical success requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including pre-training of compact architectures and data augmentation or synthesis), and theoretical understanding of when soft versus hard supervision helps. Framed this way, KD is the most practical, multi-strategy mechanism for real-world compression, provided practitioners pair it with complementary techniques and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logits-matching into a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention matching, ensemble and multi-teacher guidance, data- and teacher-free variants, and system-level integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs when teacher–student capacity, distillation targets, and data strategies are chosen thoughtfully, but its effectiveness is context-dependent: data availability, distributional shift, architecture compatibility, and task-specific behaviors can limit transfer and require tailored evaluation and mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: The Strengths and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into deployable, efficient students across modalities. Empirical work shows KD can preserve task performance while drastically reducing size and compute, but its success depends on choices of what and how to transfer, availability and provenance of data, and training dynamics. Advances in feature-matching, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer selection, data-free synthesis, and robustness-aware distillation expand KD's applicability but do not eliminate core challenges—optimization barriers, distribution heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and potential transfer of unwanted behaviors. A careful, task-aware combination of techniques is therefore required to realize reliable, compact models for production use.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, Results, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened logits to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schedules, data‑free and synthetic-data strategies, and teacher-training schemes that improve transfer. When combined with architecture-aware redesign, pruning, and quantization, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. However, practical success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals with student capacity, appropriate data strategies, and evaluation for robustness, long-tail behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework that enables transferring predictive power from large, expensive models to smaller, deployable ones. KD supports diverse practical constraints — absent training data, limited downstream-task data, domain shifts, multi-task settings, and architectural mismatches — and couples naturally with automated model search and targeted feature imitation. By viewing KD as a family of techniques (logit transfer, feature mimicking, adversarial-sample guidance, synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-ensemble strategies) practitioners can compress models while retaining or even improving task-relevant inductive structure and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and relational alignment—consistently enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while recovering much of teacher accuracy when applied with attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization dynamics. Practical KD pipelines typically combine distilled signals with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adopt data-aware strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data generation, or data-free protocols) to address real-world deployment challenges. Key open problems include robustly preserving long-tail or rare behaviors, handling distribution shift and privacy constraints, and automating student design for strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. A broad and growing set of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble schedules, data-free synthesis, and task- or architecture-aware adaptations—enables compact models to approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Effective application depends on careful teacher–student design, data strategies, and integration with complementary compression methods; open issues remain around robustness, rare-token behavior, privacy, and heterogeneous architecture alignment.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger or more complex models to smaller ones to reduce inference cost, improve deployability, or impart desirable properties (robustness, fairness, interpretability). Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, ensemble consensus, attention maps) and in what data is available (original training data, synthetic data, or no data). Practical systems combine KD with architecture-level compression (pruning, structured sparsity) and with training-time strategies (online or continual distillation, curriculum schedules) to trade off efficiency and accuracy. While KD yields strong empirical results across NLP, speech, vision, and generative models, open challenges remain in data-free settings, cross-domain generalization, preserving fairness and interpretability, and designing distillation objectives that best capture the teacher’s knowledge for a given task.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD supports domain adaptation, latency-aware architecture transformations, robustness transfer, and interpretable model surrogates. When combined with careful training protocols (e.g., multi-teacher schemes, domain adaptation, or targeted regularization), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models in resource- and latency-constrained or safety-critical settings across vision, speech, 3D perception, and natural language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models so students meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. Research across vision and language has produced diverse distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational objectives), training regimes (offline teacher supervision, online co-distillation, self-distillation, multi-teacher ensembles), and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and when attention is paid to teacher–student compatibility, data provenance, and optimization dynamics. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving long-tail or rare-token behaviors in NLP, robustness under distribution shift, and principled treatment of privacy and heterogeneity in federated or edge settings.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a system‑level component — choosing what signals to transfer, co‑designing student architectures, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with structural compression — KD delivers substantial gains in latency, memory, and deployability across vision and language tasks. KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, and careful evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints. The recommended stance is to adopt KD as a first‑line, multifunctional tool within a broader compression pipeline and to pair it with complementary methods and rigorous validation for deployment-critical properties.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Strategies, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied deliberately — choosing what form of knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle data and deployment constraints — KD routinely yields favorable tradeoffs between model compactness and retained performance. However, distillation is not automatic: data availability, teacher–student mismatches, and application-specific constraints (latency, privacy, heterogeneity) shape both achievable gains and failure modes. Best practice therefore combines representation-aware objectives, curriculum or annealing schedules, multi-teacher or ensemble guidance where helpful, and deployment-aware mechanisms such as data-free generation or privacy-preserving aggregation to realize robust, efficient students.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a system-level toolkit rather than a single loss term, KD reliably improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs across modalities and tasks. Its success depends on deliberate choices about what is transferred (logits, features, attention, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies. Important open problems remain around distribution shift, low-frequency behaviors, privacy- and data-constrained settings, and principled data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central for deploying large deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, researchers have developed logit-based distillation, feature- and attention-level mimicking, ensemble- and multi-teacher schemes, task-adaptive compression, and data- or teacher-free variants. These methods trade off compute, memory, and sometimes robustness or fairness, and are often complementary to pruning and architecture search. Practical adoption favors combinations of pretraining, targeted distillation objectives, and adaptations to mismatches between teacher and student (e.g., inputs or architecture).

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used model-compression paradigm that trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models or ensembles, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD has diversified into methods that transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, relational signals, or synthetic data; it is often combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of the teacher's performance when teacher–student capacity, data availability, and distillation targets are well aligned, but there are persistent challenges—preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher errors or bias, handling data-free scenarios, and ensuring robustness under distribution shift—that motivate task-aware and data-aware distillation designs.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models while attempting to preserve accuracy and useful inductive biases. Approaches span classic teacher–student logit matching, representation and feature imitation, layer mapping strategies for large pretrained language models, data-free and zero-shot methods that avoid access to original training data, and privacy- or communication-aware frameworks for distributed settings. Empirical work demonstrates these methods can yield practical speedups, substantial parameter reductions, and competitive task performance across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks; theoretical and empirical studies also clarify when softened teacher targets or distilled datasets best help student capacity. Remaining challenges include balancing privacy and utility, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers are large, and extending guarantees and methods across modalities and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses soft‑label (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and online schemes, self‑distillation, and data‑free synthesis. Across vision, speech, and natural language applications, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when carefully designed; its empirical success depends on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, data availability or synthesis, and complementary compression steps such as pruning or quantization. Important open issues include robustness under domain shift, preservation of rare or safety‑critical behavior, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or undesirable properties.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy and desirable properties. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and in how and when the transfer occurs (offline teacher-to-student, online/co-distillation, adversarial/ensemble-driven, or data-free with synthetic samples). Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical work shows strong gains in efficiency, but also highlights limitations: dependence on teacher quality and data alignment, possible degradation under domain shift or when sensitive attributes are transferred, and open problems in data-free or privacy-preserving settings. This synthesis summarizes key mechanisms, representative variants, cross-modal applications, common engineering practices, and the principal open challenges informed by recent empirical and survey literature.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Deployment Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) occupies a central, practical role in compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision and language applications. KD offers a flexible set of transfer signals and training regimes that—when deliberately chosen and combined with complementary compression methods—regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is context dependent: its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability and augmentation, the choice of distilled signals, and explicit checks for robustness and rare-case behavior. I argue KD should be the first-line tool in a compression pipeline but must be used together with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and targeted evaluation to avoid common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Toward Representation- and Strategy-driven Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation remains a central approach to compress large deep learning models for deployment in resource-constrained and domain-specific NLP settings. I argue that to realize reliably compact and generalizable student models we must move past sole reliance on teacher soft-labels and adopt representation-aware objectives, structured channel/feature matching, adaptive training curricula, and practical strategies for low-precision, data-limited, and privacy-sensitive scenarios. Combining these approaches yields students that better capture teacher knowledge, adapt to new domains, and meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Targeted Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, pragmatic family of techniques for converting large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels alone—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational or contrastive signals—and is commonly combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence across vision, language, generation, and graph domains shows that carefully designed KD pipelines can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost. Practical success depends on principled teacher–student co‑design, choices about what and how to transfer, data availability (including data‑free or synthetic approaches), and explicit evaluation of robustness, rare‑token or fine‑grained behaviors, and privacy risks. Despite broad empirical success, open research questions remain about theoretical characterization of what transfers, reliably preserving long‑tail behaviors, and automating tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. It delivers meaningful trade-offs between model size, latency, and retained performance when paired with appropriate distillation targets, student-aware design, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD’s success is conditional: it depends on teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability (including privacy constraints), the choice of distilled signals (soft targets versus intermediate features), and optimization practices. Best outcomes arise from task-aware distillation pipelines that combine soft-target transfer, representation-level supervision, and pragmatic strategies such as data synthesis, augmentation, or architecture-aware adjustments.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression: A Pipeline‑Oriented, Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core and first‑line strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students, but only when embedded in a carefully designed pipeline. KD’s value comes from its flexibility — it can transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and be applied offline, online, or with synthetic/data‑free inputs — and from its ability to compose with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies. Yet KD is not a universal remedy: outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality and suitability, student capacity and architecture, availability and domain match of data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy. The recommended stance is pragmatic: prioritize KD as the core compression tool, combine it with complementary structural and data techniques, adopt teacher‑aware and student‑aware design (including meta‑teaching and targeted sample strategies), and evaluate compressed models under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and distributed settings KD often recovers much of a teacher's predictive performance while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and deployment under resource or privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: outcomes depend on what signals are transferred (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, availability and quality of data (including data-free or federated setups), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats distillation as one element of a compression pipeline that combines representation matching, architecture-aware student design, data strategies, and risk-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for converting large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision and NLP, KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with careful choices of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. However, KD’s effectiveness is context-dependent: teacher quality, capacity mismatch, data availability, and deployment constraints determine whether distilled students approach teacher performance or inherit undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods include transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and data-free or few-shot variants to handle limited or private data. Best results come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that also incorporates architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. KD is therefore a central tool for efficient deployment, but it has clear limits and must be designed carefully to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or losing rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted strategy to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, KD variants have demonstrated the ability to recover much of a teacher model’s performance while substantially reducing inference latency and memory. Practical deployments treat KD as a flexible, system-level primitive—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how to expose students to training data (real, synthesized, or online), and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical successes coexist with practical limits: teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, and risks of transferring undesirable behaviors or losing robustness remain active research and engineering concerns.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of practical techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining predictive performance. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft output distributions, intermediate features, attention/relations) and how transfer is performed (offline teacher supervision, multi-teacher curricula, self-distillation, or data-free synthesis). Effective compression pipelines align distillation objectives with student capacity, leverage task- and data-aware strategies, and combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Key challenges include teacher–student mismatch, limited or no access to original training data, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and robustness under domain shift; addressing these issues requires careful selection of distilled signals, adaptive teacher weighting, and data-generation or augmentation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models. When designed with attention to what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), how teacher and student are aligned, and the data available for training, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD also integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapts to specialized settings such as multi-teacher ensembles, heterogeneous-device deployments, generative-model compression, low-precision inference, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited environments. However, KD is not uniformly automatic: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, distributional match, and design of distillation objectives and curricula.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Evidence for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) enables deployment of high-performing but large neural models by training compact student models that mimic larger teachers. Empirical work across speech, NLP, vision, and federated settings shows KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving accuracy, and its effectiveness increases when combined with complementary techniques: pre-training compact architectures, adaptive layer mapping for transformers, data-centric augmentations, ensemble teachers, and robustness-aware objectives. This paper synthesizes results from recent studies to argue that a principled KD pipeline—pre-train compact students, match representations flexibly, leverage data augmentation and teacher ensembles, and incorporate robustness or task-specific objectives—yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and performance for practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Spence
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior or internal signals. A mature family of techniques—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention, multi-teacher and online schedules, many-to-many layer mappings, and data-aware or data-free strategies—enables substantial reductions in inference cost and model size while retaining much of a teacher’s performance. Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and provenance, and training protocols; complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-specific adaptations improve outcomes. Open challenges include reliable distillation with limited or private data, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors in NLP, avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors, and principled selection of distillation targets for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Outcomes, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal signals from teachers. Over the past decade KD has broadened from simple soft-label matching to a diverse set of techniques — intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data- or generator-based synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems remain in robustness to domain shift, preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks, privacy- and data-constrained distillation, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring richer supervision from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining predictive performance. In practice KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when co-designed with student architectures, appropriate distillation signals, and complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and provenance, and careful choices about what information is transferred; it also raises privacy and robustness concerns that must be handled by task-aware pipelines. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the default, practical backbone of compression workflows while recognizing and mitigating its limits through combined methods and targeted evaluation.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels—soft output distributions, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals—and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on careful selection of what to transfer, teacher–student co‑design, data strategies (including data‑free or synthesized data), and explicit treatment of robustness, distribution shift, long‑tail behavior, and privacy. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, its effectiveness is context dependent and requires empirical validation under target deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation: Task-adaptive, Privacy-aware, and Feature-centric Compression for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are now essential tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. When applied thoughtfully—adapting to task requirements, leveraging feature-level signals, and accounting for data availability—KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while improving inference speed, memory footprint, and interpretability. However, naive distillation can fail under data heterogeneity, limited data, or strong teacher–student mismatches; addressing these requires task-aware layer selection, multi-teacher strategies, and alternatives to standard logit matching. I argue that the most effective KD pipelines combine task-adaptive compression, feature-directed supervision, and methods that preserve privacy and robustness to limited data.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Pragmatic Design Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable family of methods that enables deployment of high-performing but resource-hungry models by training compact students that retain much of teacher behavior. KD delivers major operational benefits — reduced inference latency, lower memory footprint, and greater deployability under compute, bandwidth, and privacy constraints — but it is not a one-size-fits-all cure. Real-world success requires treating KD as a design paradigm: choose what form of knowledge to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), co-design teacher and student capacities, address data limitations (via targeted augmentation or synthetic data), and explicitly manage robustness, fairness, and rare-token behaviors. When combined with complementary compression tools and careful evaluation, KD is the central practical strategy for producing efficient, reliable models for modern NLP and deep-learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical toolkit for turning large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Methods vary from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, latency, and energy, but success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, optimization choices, and targeted handling of robustness, low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive settings. Important open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, preserving rare-token and domain-specific signals, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers or data are scarce, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact students. Distillation strategies include transferring softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, distilling relational or task‑specific signals, and applying progressive or self‑distillation schedules. In practice KD is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that considers student architecture, data availability, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Remaining challenges center on data‑poor or data‑free settings, preserving rare or safety‑critical behaviors, avoiding blind transfer of biases, and developing stronger theory to predict when and how distillation succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad family of techniques—matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning intermediate features or attention maps, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—enable deployment of compact models under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance in many settings, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and alignment, and optimization details; careful method selection and combination with complementary compression techniques are therefore central to reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students that preserve most of the teacher’s capability. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single loss function, KD supports multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), and it interoperates with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization) and data strategies (data-free synthesis, synthetic/distilled training sets). However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, and explicit choices about what to transfer and how to align representations. Practitioners should therefore adopt KD as a first-line method while designing task- and deployment-aware distillation pipelines and monitoring known failure modes such as teacher error propagation, low-frequency token degradation, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches to Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed diverse strategies—teacher–student logits matching, layer-wise representation matching, adversarial sample generation, progressive module replacement, many-to-many layer mapping, and task-aware filtering—to address capacity gaps, data access limits, privacy constraints, and robustness needs. Practical deployments additionally combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and federated protocols to meet hardware and communication budgets. Empirical work shows that careful design of distillation objectives and inputs can preserve most of the teacher’s accuracy and even transfer properties such as adversarial robustness, while specialized schemes enable distillation without original training data or across continual/heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses multiple transfer targets (softened logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), operational modes (offline, online, self- or multi-teacher), and data strategies (real, augmented, synthetic, or data-free). When integrated with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware redesign, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for vision, speech, and language tasks. Its practical success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, and the provenance and match of training data materially influence outcomes. Remaining gaps include principled theory of when distillation helps, reliable transfer of robustness and fairness, preserving rare or safety-critical behaviors, and automating student-objective selection for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses supervising students with softened teacher outputs as well as transferring intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization protocols, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Important open challenges include handling data-poor or data-free settings, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage), and reliably transferring rare or fine-grained knowledge across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment in constrained environments, or impart desirable properties such as robustness or interpretability. Across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks, researchers have developed a spectrum of KD strategies — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention, or relational signals — and combined these with architecture-level compression, pretraining, and data-management strategies. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often approach teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation target, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems include reliable distillation without original data, transferring inductive biases and robustness, and handling heterogeneous or federated data and models.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for shrinking high-capacity models into smaller, deployable models while retaining much of their performance. When applied thoughtfully — with attention to what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations), how to align teachers and students (layer mapping, task-aware filters), and how to handle data constraints (data-free synthesis, federated heterogeneity, privacy) — KD enables latency- and memory-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and generative settings. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher–student capacity matching, the choice of distilled signals, and addressing data heterogeneity or absence. The evidence suggests KD should be treated as a flexible toolkit combined with complementary strategies (architecture search, quantization, data augmentation) to meet real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, pragmatic family of methods for producing compact models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. Empirical work shows KD can transfer rich supervisory signals beyond hard labels—ranging from softened logits to internal representations, attention patterns, and relational objectives—and that carefully designed distillation pipelines often recover most of a teacher’s performance while greatly reducing inference cost. In practice KD is most effective when co-designed with student architectures and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and targeted data strategies; its limits include sensitivity to teacher–student mismatch, reliance on appropriate distillation data, potential transfer of undesirable behaviors, and challenges around robustness, rare-case behavior, and privacy. These strengths and limits motivate treating KD as a core element of compression workflows rather than a universal, standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques train compact student models to emulate larger teachers, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks. The body of work spans logits- or soft-target matching, feature- and layer-wise representation transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data-free and privacy-preserving methods, and multi-teacher or progressive schemes. Empirical and theoretical studies together show KD often improves student generalization and enables substantial efficiency gains, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, and optimization choices. Practical pipelines combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search while addressing failure modes such as teacher errors, low-frequency token degradation, and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically effective strategy for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as the first-line compression method and combined with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies), KD enables deployable students across modalities while also serving as a regularizer that can improve generalization. However, KD has well-documented failure modes — teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, data-limited or privacy-constrained settings, and difficulties preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors — so practical deployment requires careful co-design of teacher signals, student capacity, and data protocols. The body of evidence supports KD as a central tool in compression pipelines but emphasizes hybrid workflows and targeted mitigations for its limits.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods include soft-output (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, and more recent data-free, multi-teacher, and online/self-distillation variants. When combined with architecture-aware transformations such as pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search, KD enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory that are critical for deploying NLP systems. Remaining challenges include distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and fine-grained behaviors, robustness under distribution shift and adversarial settings, and safeguarding fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Case for Richer Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a necessary and practical tool for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but its value depends critically on what is distilled and how. Soft-label matching transfers useful "dark knowledge" from ensembles, yet by itself often fails to capture internal structure, handle domain or data heterogeneity, or operate when original data are unavailable. Combining soft labels with internal- and feature-level guidance, architecture- and task-aware compression, and data- or privacy-aware generation strategies yields more robust, compact models that retain teacher performance across NLP and broader deep learning tasks.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from larger, richer teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature encompasses simple soft-label matching, richer supervision signals that align intermediate features or attention, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving designs, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and layer skipping. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation can both compress and regularize models, but effectiveness depends on teacher-student mismatch, data availability, and optimization choices; practical pipelines therefore combine multiple compression mechanisms, careful signal selection, and task-aware adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost and storage are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label transfer to a family of methods that include intermediate-feature matching, task-aware layer mapping, data-free and federated variants, and attention- or instance-aware strategies. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s practical value for deploying resource-constrained models, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. This synthesis summarizes prevailing approaches, practical patterns, application domains, and recurring limitations to guide future use and research.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, first‑line strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students, because it provides flexible channels of transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and composes naturally with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure: its benefits depend on teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and task- or domain-specific requirements (robustness, privacy, rare-token fidelity). A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the core toolkit, selects appropriate distillation signals and curricula, and composes KD with architecture-aware design, augmentation, and structural compression while explicitly evaluating limits under distribution shift and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone.
